index.content:
这是我的个人知识库，用 Obsidian 写，自动发布到这里。
作者 Chris Pan · GitHub · 个人主页
库里有三种页面：

地图（maps）：一个主题或一个人的入口页，把相关的笔记和来源串起来，并列出还没想清楚的问题。
笔记（notes）：一条一个想法的原子笔记，大多是中英双语，每篇都写了局限。状态都是 draft，意思是还在改。
来源（sources）：读过、看过的文章、访谈、论文的摘要和要点。原文和字幕全文不在这里发布。

可以从这几张地图开始：

张一鸣：从 2010 年的”克己”到 2021 年的”平常心”
Elon Musk：有用、第一性原理、ego/能力比
David Deutsch：知识、创造与进步
Scaling and General Methods：bitter lesson 与 scaling laws
LLM Training：推理、强化学习、reward hacking

左边的目录可以按文件夹浏览，右边的关系图谱和反向链接可以顺着链接往下读。下面是全部内容的目录。
Maps（17）

AI and Work — 主题：ai, knowledge-work, verification, coding, design；链接 24 篇笔记、4 个来源。
David Deutsch — Naval 播客里关于 David Deutsch 的 8 集，以及从中提取的笔记。（链接 8 篇笔记、8 个来源）
Elon Musk — 主题：elon-musk, first-principles, ego, risk, usefulness；链接 6 篇笔记、2 个来源，含二手说法与一手原话的对照。
Learning — 主题：learning, specific-knowledge；链接 12 篇笔记、8 个来源。
Life — 主题：life, happiness, health, relationships, consciousness；链接 16 篇笔记、8 个来源。
LLM Agents — 主题：ai, llm, agents, harness, skills；链接 28 篇笔记、6 个来源。
LLM Training — 主题：ai, llm, reinforcement-learning, reasoning, evaluation；链接 49 篇笔记、8 个来源。
Nassim Taleb — 主题：taleb, risk, asymmetry, skin-in-the-game, feedback；边读《非对称风险》边建，目前 1 个来源、2 个 Naval 转述；链接 1 篇笔记，其余模型待提取。
Naval Archive — Index of public posts imported from nav.al as observed on 2026-04-13.（链接 2 篇笔记、232 个来源）
Note-taking — 主题：note-taking, knowledge；链接 5 篇笔记、3 个来源。
Prompt Optimization — 主题：prompt-optimization, llm, apo；链接 14 篇笔记、8 个来源。
Scaling and General Methods — 主题：ai, scaling, compute, scaling-laws；链接 12 篇笔记、3 个来源。
Specific Knowledge — 主题：specific-knowledge, judgment, leverage；链接 9 篇笔记、9 个来源。
Steph Ango — 主题：authors, note-taking, writing；链接 5 篇笔记、8 个来源。
Wealth — 主题：wealth, ownership, leverage；链接 13 篇笔记、11 个来源。
Writing — 主题：writing, thinking；链接 3 篇笔记、3 个来源。
张一鸣 — 主题：zhang-yiming, delayed-gratification, self-deception, equanimity, learning；链接 13 篇笔记、3 个来源，含 2010 年微博与 2021 年演讲、全员信的前后对照。

Notes（209）
按主题分组。分组只为导航，不代表已有对应 map；括号里是该组已挂的 map。
笔记方法与写作（9）

Files outlast tools — The durable unit of a knowledge system should be the file, because applications change faster than formats. draft
Links make notes compound — Links turn isolated notes into reusable thinking objects that can accumulate value over time. draft
Atomic notes should capture one reusable idea — An atomic note is most useful when it captures a single idea that can be reused, linked, and revised independently. draft
Automation should support understanding — Automation is useful when it reduces clerical work without taking interpretation and judgment away from the human. draft
Structure should emerge from use — A note system stays lighter when structure is added in response to actual use instead of up-front taxonomy design. draft
Concise notes are easier to reuse — Short clear notes are easier to connect, scan, and repurpose than sprawling explanations. draft
Style is a constraint that reduces decision load — Consistent conventions reduce the number of small choices required to keep a writing system coherent. draft
Naval’s writing is organized as an archive of reusable principles — The site presents ideas less as chronological blogging and more as a reusable archive of compact principles, podcast essays, and recurring mental models. draft
Podcast transcripts can function like essays when they are tightly edited — When spoken material is tightly curated, the transcript can work like a written essay and become much easier to reuse as a source note. draft

财富、杠杆与判断（16）

Wealth is ownership of assets that work without your immediate labor — Wealth is not just income or cash on hand but control over productive assets that continue to generate value when you are not actively working. draft
Ownership breaks the linear trade between time and income — Selling labor can produce a good living, but ownership is what allows returns to scale beyond the number of hours you can personally supply. draft
Status and wealth obey different games — Wealth can be created in positive-sum systems, while status is usually positional and invites comparison, rivalry, and distraction. draft
Real wealth comes from long-term value creation rather than shortcuts — Promises of instant riches usually reveal a seller’s business model, while durable wealth is more often the result of patient compounding and real value creation. draft
Judgment compounds when paired with leverage — Good judgment matters more when code, capital, media, or people let one decision propagate far beyond a single hour of labor, because leverage scales the downside of bad decisions alongside the… draft
Building and selling are complementary forms of leverage — Building creates value, while selling distributes, funds, and amplifies it; the combination is unusually powerful because each side multiplies the other. draft
Permissionless leverage lets individuals scale without gatekeepers — Code and media are unusually powerful forms of leverage because they can be deployed without first being granted authority over employees or capital, allowing one person to reach and influence far… draft
Accountability turns reputation into leverage — When someone takes visible risks under their own name, they make failure more painful but also make success easier for other people to trust, fund, follow, and reward. draft
Business models compound faster when they combine scale economies low marginal cost and network effects — Some businesses are structurally easier to scale because each additional unit costs less to produce, copies can be distributed almost for free, and new users increase the value of the system for… draft
Productizing yourself means scaling authentic specific knowledge — The strongest leverage often comes from turning what is genuinely distinctive about a person into a repeatable product, medium, or system rather than performing a generic role slightly better than… draft
Freedom depends on both earnings and low fixed needs — Higher income helps, but freedom grows much faster when recurring obligations stay low enough that you can refuse bad options. draft
Luck matters less when you become repeatedly opportunity-ready — Preparation, motion, and distinctive reputation can make favorable breaks more frequent and more recognizable, reducing dependence on blind luck. draft
Scale often requires removing variation rather than adding features — Systems usually become more robust at scale when unnecessary complexity is stripped away rather than when more options are layered on. draft
The idiot index exposes how much of a price is process inefficiency — Finished price divided by raw-material cost: a high ratio says the price is mostly process, and process can be redesigned. draft
Usefulness is how much you help people times how many people you reach — Musk’s test for a project: if it works, how useful will it be, to how many people; aspire to work, not glory. draft
First principles reasoning replaces precedent with the constituent elements of a problem — Break a problem into its constituent elements and reason up, instead of assuming the next rocket costs what past rockets cost. draft

学习与特定知识（10）

Learning deepens when action creates demand — Concrete work generates better questions, stronger motivation, and more durable learning than study pursued in a vacuum. draft
Curiosity makes it easier to learn from other people — When someone stops trying to appear competent and starts asking sincere questions, other people are often more willing to explain what they know in practical detail. draft
A student mindset makes uncertainty easier to navigate — Career ambiguity becomes easier to tolerate when a person treats each job, project, city, and conversation as part of an ongoing learning process rather than as proof that they have already figured… draft
Principles become useful only in context — General principles help only after direct experience teaches where they apply, where they fail, and what they are actually pointing at. draft
Specific knowledge is mostly discovered rather than taught — The capabilities that make a person unusually valuable usually emerge through action, pattern recognition, and lived context rather than through standardized instruction or abstract self-analysis… draft
Specific knowledge emerges where capability and authenticity overlap — People often become hardest to replace where their natural style, repeated competence, and real preferences reinforce one another. draft
Specific knowledge often accumulates at the frontier where training is incomplete — The more a field is moving, creative, or technical, the less likely its most valuable knowledge can be fully packaged into standard instruction. draft
Specific knowledge becomes more valuable as AI commoditizes routine coding — As AI coding tools commoditize routine boilerplate and repetitive implementation, the value of specific knowledge — deep domain expertise, architectural judgment, and the ability to specify and… draft
High-value work sits where out-of-distribution judgment meets leverage — Durable high-value work needs two axes at once, not one. The first axis is how out-of-distribution the work is — how hard your output is to compress into training data (novel problems, messy… draft
The only durable moat against AI is being an out-of-distribution human — Most work lives in the fat middle of the bell curve: tasks that repeat with small variation, which is exactly what models train on (logs, emails, code, recordings of someone doing the job). draft

人生、幸福与心智（13）

A good life must be earned across mind body and relationships — Peace, physical vitality, and loving relationships are separate achievements that cannot be outsourced to financial success. draft
Desire creates a self-imposed deficit state — Strong wanting often turns the present into a problem to be solved, making unhappiness part of the price of fixation. draft
多巴胺编码的是奖励和惩罚 — 多巴胺不是快乐分子，它不负责”喜欢”（liking）——对奖励的享受由独立的脑区系统处理。 draft
Material comfort removes some sources of unhappiness but does not complete the job — Money can buy freedom from many forms of stress, but it does not automatically produce peace, fitness, love, or inner coherence. draft
Happiness is a trainable state grounded in understanding — Happiness is less like acquiring one decisive reward and more like learning to see clearly enough that unnecessary inner conflict relaxes. draft
Elusive outcomes are often best pursued indirectly — Competitive or subtle goals such as wealth, happiness, and status often arrive more reliably as byproducts of the right process than as objects chased directly. draft
Self-directed work can dissolve the work-life boundary — When work is self-directed and deeply aligned, it often stops feeling like a separate compartment even though it can also consume far more of life. draft
Fearing failure rejects success because both share one path — Success and failure are not two forks in the road; they are two possible outcomes of the same action, and you cannot claim one while refusing the other. draft
Ego is friction on execution rather than the source of drive — Ego-driven emotions are handles others can pull and internal drag on the work itself, so removing them makes execution cleaner, not weaker. draft
The self is an illusion generated by thoughts appearing in consciousness — Naval identifies enlightenment behaviorally, not by self-report: watch someone long enough for something genuinely bad to happen to them, and if there is “not even a perturbation,” that is how you… draft
An ego larger than ability cuts the feedback loop with reality — Musk’s ego to ability ratio: an ego above ability makes you filter out criticism, breaking the feedback loop with reality. draft
Treating failure as the expected outcome makes a low-probability bet bearable — Musk rated SpaceX and Tesla below 10% to succeed and expected to lose the money, which freed him to go all in. draft
Not retaliating keeps future options open because you cannot know who will help you — Musk gave way in the PayPal coup and kept the relationships; eight years later the same people’s fund helped save SpaceX. draft

张一鸣：成长与平常心（13，已挂 map：张一鸣）

Delayed gratification is how deep you are willing to stay with a problem — 张一鸣早期微博里的延迟满足感不是先忍住，而是愿意在一个问题上停留多深、不被第一反应牵着走。 draft
Vague words hide unresolved thinking and protect self-deception — 含糊的词替换掉的正是还没想清楚或有分歧的部分；张一鸣把含糊看作侥幸和自我欺骗。 draft
Many complex problems are projections of a simpler problem one level up — 很多复杂问题是更高维度上一个简单问题的投影，根上的解法简单但需要更大的决心。 draft
Over-abstraction is leverage on thinking that magnifies a wrong premise — 过度抽象和随便 all-in 都是捷径；抽象是思维杠杆，前提错了就被放大，张一鸣称之为理性的自负。 draft
Caring too much about the outcome distorts the action — 平常心：对结果执着太重会让动作变形，标签和预期也一样；去掉中间的损耗。 draft
After a mistake realize it correct it learn from it then forgive it — 失误四部曲 realize、correct、learn、forgive；归因要诚实，不把运气当能力，不长时间自我指责。 draft
Honesty pays in long games because duplicity gets more expensive as information flows — 张一鸣用经济理由论证诚实：长期交往里说话实在有溢价，工作就是积累信誉。 draft
A CEO at the center of a growing organization drifts into an internal view — CEO 的负规模效应：中心节点陷入汇报和审批，知识停止更新；张一鸣据此卸任去学习。 draft
Laziness comes in physical mental and emotional forms and self-control resists all three — 懒惰分体力、思考、情绪三种，修炼多是克服惰性；地基是体力、睡眠和注意力的开源节流。 draft
Waiting for certainty is itself a decision because confidence never reaches one hundred percent — 确信度永远到不了 100%，等待本身就是决定；不动肯定是错，先做有用又没错的事。 draft
Hunger has three levels greed achievement and curiosity — 饥渴分贪婪、成就动机、好奇心三层，对应投机者、攀登者、探索者；强烈的动机比方法更根本。 draft
Confidence is staying active while knowing your shortcomings — 谦虚是看到不足，自信是知道不足仍然积极；惰性、拖拉常来自不自信，安全感来自阶段目标的实现。 draft
Things that are hard to keep doing well usually lack a metric — 难坚持的事往往缺指标；提炼指标就是分解事物，且要常测量，否则反馈来得太晚。 draft

David Deutsch：知识、创造与进步（8）

Progress is possible but not inevitable — Deutsch’s optimism claims that problems are soluble, not that they will be solved. draft
Creativity is not just recombination — Asked about Steve Jobs’s “creativity is just connecting things,” Deutsch says the only false word is “just.” Saying “Einstein only recombined existing geometry” is like saying “humans are only… draft
Bayesian updating ranks existing theories but cannot create new ones — Bayes’ theorem redistributes credence among hypotheses that someone has already written down. draft
An experiment chooses between rival explanations — Deutsch separates three activities that are all loosely called “experiments.” An experiment tests two rival explanations against each other when you cannot tell without it which is better. draft
Explanatory creativity can cross gaps that evolution cannot — Biological evolution and human thought both create knowledge by variation and selection, but evolution has no foresight. draft
Education is the most anti-rational institution because it exists to transmit faithfully — Deutsch’s biological analogy: the most evolutionarily frozen parts of a cell are the genetic code and the ribosome, the cell’s “educational institution,” whose only job is to pass knowledge to the… draft
Preserving the means of error correction is the heart of morality — Mistakes don’t require malevolence. They are “the normal condition of humans,” and well-intentioned errors that nobody can yet see as errors are as dangerous as bad actors. draft
Choose problems that are fun whether or not you solve them — David Deutsch’s “fun criterion” is a rule for selecting problems, not a rule about doing only what feels pleasant. draft

Nassim Taleb：风险共担（1，已挂 map：Nassim Taleb）

Systems learn by removing the parts that fail — Taleb: “Systems learn by removing parts, via negativa.” A system improves because the bad parts drop out, not because they get wiser; skin in the game keeps that removal working. draft

AI 与知识工作、组织（11，已挂 map：AI and Work）

AI knowledge work improves when context is consolidated — General knowledge work stays difficult for AI when the relevant context is scattered across tools, documents, metrics, and unwritten institutional memory. draft
Context consolidation and verifiability reinforce each other — When context is unified, it becomes easier to judge whether output matches intent; when evaluation is clearer, it becomes easier to decide which context actually matters. draft
Organizations can use AI as a load-bearing context layer — If AI can maintain context across workflows and surface decisions when needed, companies may rely less on meetings and hierarchy as their primary coordination mechanism. draft
New infrastructure changes scale before it changes culture — When a new infrastructure layer arrives, the first visible effect is often a change in scale and operating rhythm, with new cultural norms only becoming legible later. draft
Most AI adoption still imitates old tools instead of redesigning workflows — Early technology adoption often wraps new capability in familiar interfaces, which makes transition easier but also delays deeper organizational redesign. draft
Managers in AI-native organizations may become designers of verification systems — If agents can generate and execute more work, one of management’s highest-value functions may shift toward defining standards, exceptions, checkpoints, and escalation paths rather than directly… draft
AI-native knowledge work is a verification problem before it is an intelligence problem — The biggest barrier to agentic knowledge work is often not generation quality but the absence of tight feedback loops that show whether output is actually correct, useful, or complete. draft
Verification quality determines how safely work can be delegated — Delegation becomes safer when the recipient’s output can be checked quickly and reliably, which is why tasks with clear tests scale to agents more easily than tasks with ambiguous quality signals. draft
Work becomes easier to automate when evaluation criteria are externalized — As soon as a team’s standards can be expressed in tests, rubrics, checklists, or observable outcomes, more of the work becomes legible to automation instead of remaining trapped in tacit judgment. draft
Weak feedback loops push humans back into low-leverage review work — When output quality is hard to verify, humans end up re-checking intermediate work manually, which collapses agentic leverage back into expensive serial supervision. draft
Humans should supervise AI from leveraged positions rather than sit inside every loop — Human oversight creates more value when it sets direction, reviews outcomes, and intervenes at high-leverage points than when it manually clears every intermediate step. draft

AI 编程（9，已挂 map：AI and Work）

LLM coding usefulness came from crossing a reliability threshold, not raw capability — LLMs became useful for coding not because they got dramatically smarter but because they became reliable enough to run inside automated feedback loops. draft
Near-term AI productivity gains come from retooling the industry rather than better models — If LLMs became useful by crossing a reliability threshold rather than by getting smarter, then further model improvements alone are unlikely to deliver a 10x productivity jump over the previous… draft
AI productivity claims conflict between anecdotal reports and formal studies — Anecdotal reports of 10x productivity gains from AI coding tools conflict sharply with formal studies that show minimal or no measurable gains. draft
AI coding tools create a K-shaped workforce split between augmented engineers and those unable to leverage them — AI coding tools amplify existing skill differentials rather than flattening them. draft
A working implementation now signals twenty percent done rather than eighty percent — When code was written by hand, reaching a working implementation meant a task was roughly 80% complete. draft
LLM-generated code is locally functional but globally incoherent — LLM-generated code tends to be technically passable in isolation but architecturally incoherent across a codebase. draft
Effective AI coding treats output as hypotheses to be validated rather than code to review — The most effective AI coding workflow reframes LLM output not as code to be reviewed, but as hypotheses to be validated. draft
Spec-driven development is rising as AI shifts coding toward writing clear requirements — Effective AI coding requires writing unambiguous, formal specifications — sometimes described as “formal letter to British throne” level clarity — because the LLM will fill any ambiguity with… draft
The cognitive load of reviewing AI output is real and different from writing code — Reviewing AI-generated code imposes a cognitive load that is qualitatively different from writing code yourself. draft

AI 设计工具（4，已挂 map：AI and Work）

Conversational design tools widen exploration by lowering prototype cost — When prototyping becomes conversational, teams can test many more directions before committing to one. draft
Design systems compound when AI can apply them automatically — A design system becomes more operationally valuable when an AI tool can absorb it and reuse it across every new draft by default. draft
Design handoff improves when design intent travels with implementation context — Implementation handoff gets stronger when it includes the reasoning and interaction intent behind a design rather than only a static artifact. draft
AI creative workflows get stronger when import refinement export and handoff stay connected — AI creative tools become more useful when they collapse multiple workflow stages into one continuous surface. draft

Prompt 工程与自动优化（14，已挂 map：Prompt Optimization）

APO 的核心落地建议 — APO 最值得落地的地方，不是“让模型帮你写一个更漂亮的 prompt”，而是把 prompt 调优变成一个有样本、有指标、有候选集、有迭代记录的工程流程。 draft
Prompt optimization turns prompt writing into measurable search — Automatic prompt optimization replaces manual trial-and-error with a loop that generates prompt candidates, evaluates them against examples, and keeps variants that improve a task metric. draft
APO systems share a five-stage optimization anatomy — APO systems can be compared by how they initialize seed prompts, evaluate behavior and feedback, generate candidate prompts, filter promising candidates, and decide iteration depth. draft
APO quality depends on validation data and metric design — APO can only optimize what its validation set and objective function make visible. draft
Prompt optimization spaces can be discrete continuous or hybrid — Prompt optimization is not one technique because the object being optimized can differ: human-readable instructions, selected examples, annotations, soft prompt embeddings, or mixed prompt programs. draft
Automatic prompt engineering treats instructions as programs — APE treats natural-language instructions as programs that a model executes. draft
Seedless prompt induction lowers entry cost but still needs task examples — Seedless prompt induction removes the need for a human-authored starting prompt by inferring instructions from input-output examples. draft
Textual gradients make prompt errors editable in natural language — Textual-gradient APO converts prompt failures into natural-language critiques, then asks an LLM to edit the prompt away from those failure modes. draft
Human-in-the-loop prompt optimization preserves domain judgment — Human-in-the-loop APO keeps the search benefits of automated prompt variation while letting users judge domain fit, readability, explanation quality, and tradeoffs that are not fully captured by a… draft
Agent prompt optimization must search patterns as well as wording — For LLM agents, prompt quality is shaped by the surrounding pattern as much as by instruction wording. draft
Few-shot prompt performance swings wildly with example choice and order — Studies of in-context learning find that prompt format, the chosen training examples, and their order can change performance from near-random guessing to near state-of-the-art. draft
Chain-of-thought pays off only for complex reasoning in large models — Chain-of-thought prompting generates step-by-step reasoning chains before the answer, but its benefits are pronounced mainly on complicated reasoning tasks with large models (e.g. over 50B… draft
Prompt explanations fail by being nonfactual rather than inconsistent — Ye & Durrett found that including explanations in few-shot prompts brings only small-to-moderate gains on reasoning-over-text tasks, and the dominant failure mode is nonfactual explanations rather… draft
Self-consistency sampling improves reliability through majority vote — Instead of decoding one answer, self-consistency samples multiple reasoning paths at temperature > 0 and selects the majority answer, which consistently improves reasoning accuracy. draft

LLM Agent 架构与 harness（14，已挂 map：LLM Agents）

An LLM agent combines planning memory and tool use around a language model core — An LLM-powered agent uses the language model as its brain and adds three components: planning (decompose goals into subgoals, reflect on mistakes), memory (short-term in-context learning plus… draft
An agent’s short-term memory is its context window and long-term memory is external retrieval — The mapping to human memory is direct: sensory memory maps to learned embeddings of raw inputs, short-term (working) memory maps to in-context learning and is bounded by the finite context window… draft
Finite context length forces agent design to work within limited communication bandwidth — The context window is the scarce resource in agent design: it must hold conversation history, detailed instructions, API call context, and responses all at once. draft
Tool use is bottlenecked by knowing when and how to call rather than by the tools themselves — Equipping an LLM with tools is easy; the hard part is the model deciding reliably whether a tool is needed, which one, and with what arguments. draft
Keep a tool call only when it improves prediction of future tokens — Toolformer learns to use external tools self-supervised: after the model annotates candidate API calls, each call is executed and kept only if inserting its result reduces the language-modeling loss… draft
Self-reflection turns trial and error into within-episode learning — Frameworks like Reflexion let an agent critique its own past actions, detect when a trajectory is inefficient or hallucinated, and reset to try again — converting trial and error into iterative… draft
LLMs cannot reliably evaluate their own output in expert domains — In ChemCrow, LLM-based scoring judged GPT-4 and the tool-augmented ChemCrow nearly equivalent, while human experts rating task completion and chemical correctness found ChemCrow far superior. draft
The harness layer around a model matters as much as its raw intelligence — A harness is the system surrounding a base model that orchestrates execution: how the model thinks and plans, calls tools and acts, perceives and manages context, stores artifacts, and evaluates… draft
A harness should keep durable state in files rather than in context — In long-horizon agent runs, artifacts such as experiment logs, code diffs, error traces, and past trajectories quickly outgrow the context window, so a harness should keep durable state in the file… draft
Context should be maintained as an evolving playbook not an appended log — Naively appending every tool response and model generation to the context grows out of control as task horizons lengthen. draft
Code is the universal language for optimizing agent harnesses — A harness is ultimately code that programs how prompts, tool calls, subagents, control flow, memory, and workflow logic work together, so an LLM that can edit that code accesses a far larger design… draft
Harness edits must be falsifiable and the evaluator must stay outside the loop — When a program is allowed to edit its own harness, abstraction boundaries break, so the editable surface must be bounded and the verifier, tracer, and permission controls must live outside the… draft
Recursive self-improvement only works above a base-model capability threshold — STOP (Self-Taught Optimizer) improved mean downstream performance across iterations with GPT-4 but degraded with weaker models like GPT-3.5 and Mixtral: recursive structure alone is not enough… draft
Repeated agent corrections belong in the codebase rather than the conversation — Agent 倾向沿用上下文里已有的模式，所以仓库里的现有代码同时是下一次生成的示范。 draft

Agent loop 工程（Pi）（7，已挂 map：LLM Agents）

A stateless loop core plus a stateful wrapper separates orchestration from session state — Pi’s agent loop is a stateless function: it receives a context snapshot and a config, emits events, and returns new messages without remembering anything between calls. draft
Inject policy through hooks so the agent loop stays product-agnostic — Pi’s loop contains no product logic. Context compaction, permission prompts, API key refresh, model switching, and graceful shutdown all live in nine config hooks — transformContext, beforeToolCall… draft
Snapshot boundaries between loop and state owner give crash safety for free — The Agent class hands the loop a shallow copy of its messages and tools on each run. draft
Stream partial messages in place so interrupted contexts stay structurally complete — During streaming, pi pushes the partial assistant message into the context array immediately and replaces that same slot as deltas arrive, swapping in the finalized message at the end. draft
Agent loops should encode failures as error tool results instead of throwing exceptions — In pi’s loop, no failure path throws. Unknown tools, invalid arguments, blocked permissions, and tool execution exceptions all become error tool-result messages fed back to the model, letting the… draft
Truncated LLM output should fail all tool calls rather than execute salvaged arguments — When an LLM response stops with reason “length”, streamed tool-call arguments are finalized by a best-effort JSON salvage parser: they may parse and validate yet be silently incomplete. draft

Steph Ango（8）

Steph Ango - Concise explanations accelerate progress — Clear short explanations reduce ambiguity and make ideas easier to transfer and combine.
Steph Ango - Don’t delegate understanding — Outsourcing too much interpretation weakens direct comprehension.
Steph Ango - Evergreen notes turn ideas into objects that you can manipulate — Ideas become more useful when they are broken into small reusable notes that can be linked, compared, and recombined.
Steph Ango - File over app — The durable unit of knowledge should be the file, because apps change faster than formats.
Steph Ango - How I use Obsidian — Steph Ango describes a low-overhead, file-first note system that favors links, search, and emergent structure over deep folder trees.
Steph Ango - Notes Thinking Model — 综合 Steph Ango 的 vault、evergreen notes、file over app 等文章，整理出他的笔记思考模型。
Steph Ango - Style is consistent constraint — Consistent constraints reduce decision overhead and make output easier to maintain.

Lilian Weng（10）

Weng - Adversarial Attacks on LLMs — A survey of adversarial attacks on LLMs at inference time, assuming fixed model weights.
Weng - Diffusion Models for Video Generation — A survey of diffusion models for video generation, organized around two strategies.
Weng - Extrinsic Hallucinations in LLMs — This post surveys extrinsic hallucination in LLMs — cases where model output is fabricated and grounded by neither the provided context nor world knowledge.
Weng - Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement — This post frames harness engineering as the near-term engine of recursive self-improvement (RSI).
Weng - LLM Powered Autonomous Agents — A foundational overview of building autonomous agents with an LLM as the core controller.
Weng - Prompt Engineering — A survey of prompt engineering for autoregressive LLMs — methods for steering model behavior without updating weights.
Weng - Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning — A comprehensive survey of reward hacking — when an RL agent exploits flaws or ambiguities in the reward function to earn high reward without completing the intended task.
Weng - Scaling Laws, Carefully — A careful review of scaling laws in deep learning — how test loss L decays as a power law with model size N, dataset size D, and compute C (C ≈ 6ND).
Weng - Thinking about High-Quality Human Data — A practical survey of collecting and curating high-quality human-annotated data, the fuel of supervised and alignment training.
Weng - Why We Think — The post surveys why and how “thinking time” (test-time compute) improves LLM reasoning.

Stanford CS336 - Lecture 01 - Overview, Tokenization — Percy Liang opens the third edition of CS336 by arguing why researchers should understand language models at the level of implementation rather than prompting, and what parts of that understanding…
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 02 - PyTorch (einops) — This is the resource accounting lecture: how to predict, before running anything, how much memory a model needs and how long a computation will take.
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 03 - Architectures — Tatsunori Hashimoto surveys modern transformer architectures by comparing what a large number of released models actually do, on the argument that no single paper gives enough detail and the design…
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 04 - Attention Alternatives — The second architecture lecture, covering two advanced departures from the vanilla transformer: linear-time alternatives to attention, and mixture of experts.
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 05 - GPUs, TPUs — The opening lecture of the systems portion of the course. It builds a hardware mental model of the GPU, contrasts it with the TPU, then works through the specific tricks that determine whether code…
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 06 - Kernels, Triton, XLA — A hands-on continuation of the GPU lecture, moving from hardware concepts to actual kernel code.
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 07 - Parallelism — The first of two parallelism lectures, taught by Percy Liang, introducing the mechanics of multi-GPU training from the ground up.
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 08 - Parallelism — The second parallelism lecture, taught by Tatsunori Hashimoto, moving from the mechanics of the previous lecture to the full modern toolbox and how practitioners combine it.
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 09 - Scaling Laws — The first of two scaling-law lectures, taught by Tatsunori Hashimoto, covering the basics before a later advanced session on muP and optimizers.
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 10 - Inference — A one-lecture treatment of inference, placed between the two scaling-law lectures.
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 11 - Scaling Laws — The second scaling lecture, deliberately a grab bag of the practical details that come after the classical Kaplan and Chinchilla material covered earlier in the course.
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 12 - Evaluation — The lecture that bridges modelling and data, on the grounds that you cannot choose training data without first deciding what behaviour you want.
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 13 - Data (Sources, Datasets) — First of two data lectures, covering where pre-training data comes from and which datasets the field has actually used.
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 14 - Data — Second of two data lectures, covering the processing pipeline rather than the sources.

Stanford CS336 - Lecture 17 - Alignment - Multimodality — Originally planned as more reinforcement learning, this lecture was reallocated to an overview of multimodal models on the grounds that the course would be incomplete without them.
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 18 - Guest Lecture - Dan Fu — A guest lecture on what happens after training: serving models, or turning electricity into tokens.

maps/AI-and-Work.title: AI and Work
maps/AI-and-Work.content:
AI 怎样改变知识工作、编程和设计工作。分节沿用 index 的三个主题组：AI 与知识工作、组织，AI 编程，AI 设计工具。
Core Ideas
Verification is the bottleneck

AI-native knowledge work is a verification problem before it is an intelligence problem — the synthesis: what is missing is a feedback loop that shows whether output is right, not more raw intelligence.
Verification quality determines how safely work can be delegated — work moves to agents as fast as its output can be checked quickly and reliably.
Work becomes easier to automate when evaluation criteria are externalized — once standards live in tests, rubrics or checklists, automation can read them.
Weak feedback loops push humans back into low-leverage review work — when output is hard to verify, humans end up re-checking every intermediate step.
Humans should supervise AI from leveraged positions rather than sit inside every loop — set direction, review outcomes and step in at high-leverage points.
Managers in AI-native organizations may become designers of verification systems — management shifts toward standards, exceptions, checkpoints and escalation paths.

Context and organizations

AI knowledge work improves when context is consolidated — knowledge work stays hard for AI while context is scattered across tools, documents and unwritten memory.
Context consolidation and verifiability reinforce each other — unified context makes output easier to judge; clear evaluation shows which context matters.
Organizations can use AI as a load-bearing context layer — AI that carries context could take over coordination now done by meetings and hierarchy.
Most AI adoption still imitates old tools instead of redesigning workflows — new capability gets wrapped in familiar interfaces, which delays deeper redesign.
New infrastructure changes scale before it changes culture — a new infrastructure layer changes scale and rhythm first; new norms show up later.

AI coding

LLM coding usefulness came from crossing a reliability threshold, not raw capability — models became useful once they were reliable enough to run inside automated feedback loops.
Near-term AI productivity gains come from retooling the industry rather than better models — the next gains come from changing how software gets built, not from smarter models alone.
AI productivity claims conflict between anecdotal reports and formal studies — anecdotes report 10x; formal studies find small or no measurable gains.
AI coding tools create a K-shaped workforce split between augmented engineers and those unable to leverage them — the tools widen existing skill gaps instead of flattening them.
A working implementation now signals twenty percent done rather than eighty percent — a working version used to mean most of the job was done; now it is the start.
LLM-generated code is locally functional but globally incoherent — passable in isolation, architecturally inconsistent across a codebase.
Effective AI coding treats output as hypotheses to be validated rather than code to review — treat model output as hypotheses checked by executable tests, not as code to read line by line.
Spec-driven development is rising as AI shifts coding toward writing clear requirements — the model fills every ambiguity, so the work moves into unambiguous specifications.
The cognitive load of reviewing AI output is real and different from writing code — reviewing generated code is a different kind of effort from writing it.

AI design tools

Conversational design tools widen exploration by lowering prototype cost — cheaper prototypes let teams try more directions before committing.
Design systems compound when AI can apply them automatically — a design system is worth more when the tool applies it to every new draft by default.
Design handoff improves when design intent travels with implementation context — hand off the reasoning and interaction intent, not only a static artifact.
AI creative workflows get stronger when import refinement export and handoff stay connected — the gain comes from collapsing several workflow stages into one surface.

Related Sources

Ivan Zhao - Steam, Steel, and Infinite Minds
Jacob O’Bryant - 2x, not 10x - Coding with LLMs in 2026
Hacker News - We might all be AI engineers now
Anthropic - Introducing Claude Design by Anthropic Labs

Open Threads

If verification is the bottleneck, which kinds of non-coding work can be given tests, rubrics or observable outcomes first?
Anecdotes say 10x and studies say little: is the gap about measurement, task mix, or who is using the tools? See AI productivity claims conflict between anecdotal reports and formal studies.
Does specific knowledge gain value as AI commoditizes routine coding, or are out-of-distribution people only late on the automation curve? Compare Specific knowledge becomes more valuable as AI commoditizes routine coding and The only durable moat against AI is being an out-of-distribution human (lint C5).

maps/David-Deutsch.title: David Deutsch
maps/David-Deutsch.content:
Naval 播客里关于 David Deutsch 的 8 集，以及从中提取的笔记。YouTube 播放列表：www.youtube.com/playlist
Core Ideas

Progress is possible but not inevitable
Creativity is not just recombination
Explanatory creativity can cross gaps that evolution cannot
Bayesian updating ranks existing theories but cannot create new ones
An experiment chooses between rival explanations
Preserving the means of error correction is the heart of morality
Education is the most anti-rational institution because it exists to transmit faithfully
Choose problems that are fun whether or not you solve them

Related Sources
系列分三个阶段。前两集 Deutsch 不在场，是 Naval 和 Brett Hall 对书的解读；后六集是 Deutsch 本人的说法。













































































#集发布时长参与者一句话1BoI Part 12021-071:06Naval, Brett好解释、知识皆猜想、反归纳、多重宇宙、悲观为何显得严肃2BoI Part 22021-120:53Naval, Brett反贝叶斯、人的独特性、费米悖论、资源是知识的函数3Human Race 12023-020:44Naval, Deutsch篝火、纠错与道德、AGI 与不服从、TCS、好解释的定义4Human Race 22023-080:34三人实验/演示/测量、简单性、反 Kuhn、英国启蒙5Deutsch Files I2024-010:55三人ChatGPT、创造力不可定义、乐趣标准、文明的威胁6Deutsch Files II2024-011:14三人四根支柱、自由意志、财富、constructor theory、进步不必然7Deutsch Files III2024-020:59三人创造力≠重组、TCS 的两个反驳、双胞胎、莫扎特8Deutsch Files IV2024-101:25三人constructor theory、量子计算机起源、反理性模因、教育
nav.al 把前两集切成了 52 篇短帖，已在 vault 里，列在第 1、2 集 source note 的 Excerpt Posts 部分。
Deutsch 本人的修正
后几集里 Deutsch 明确收回或纠正了一些前面出现过的说法：

“进步是必然的”：第 1 集把他的世界观概括成这句话，他在 Files II（1:08:37）说这种想法很危险。问题可以解决，但不保证会被解决。→ Progress is possible but not inevitable
“科学每经历一场葬礼就前进一步”：Naval 在第 1 集引用 Planck 的这句话，他在 Human Race 2（16:08）说代际更替的叙事是纯属虚构，解释不了人为什么换理论。
“多重宇宙解决了自由意志”：这是他自己在《The Fabric of Reality》里的暗示，在 Files II（34:20）和 Files IV（18:05）两次收回。
“狭窄而冒险的预测”是好解释的标志：Naval 的归纳。他说这是波普尔的表述，他不太喜欢，因为检验的对象是解释，不是预测（Human Race 1，32:19）。
给孩子打”坚实的认识论基础”：Naval 的说法。他指出波普尔认识论本身也不是坚实的基础（Human Race 2）。
“波普尔证明了 AI 不能超级智能”：记者的转述，他否认说过（Files III，0:00）。

前两集的问题，在后几集的回应








































问题前面的说法Deutsch 的回应创造性猜想从哪来第 1 集：大胆猜测、淘汰失败创造力无法定义（Files I）；不只是重组（Files III）；解释性猜想能跳过进化跳不过的缺口（Human Race 1 篝火、Files III 尾翼）；起点是问题，也就是想法之间的冲突（Files II）；他也不知道具体机制（Files III）贝叶斯与归纳第 1–2 集：贝叶斯不产生新解释水星的观测也是理论，“未知行星”可以被精确定位再排除，最后只剩爱因斯坦一个好解释（Files II）；简单性不是先验的，Solomonoff 不成立（Human Race 2）数学的确定性第 1 集：数学也会错数学与其他领域只在研究对象上不同，获得知识的方式一样（Files III）多重宇宙第 1 集：双缝干涉非局域性只出现在坍缩理论里（Human Race 1）；物理学家的抵制源自内部（Files II）；量子计算机本是为检验 Everett 而想出来的（Files IV）人的独特性 / AGI第 2 集：加算力不产生 AGIChatGPT 没有理解、没有创造力（Files I）；不存在 ASI（Files I）；人格没有等级（Files I）；AGI 复制不会爆炸（Files III）乐观与悲观第 1 集：悲观显得严肃唯一的生存威胁来自内部（Files I）；反理性模因（Files IV）；纠错强的系统能承受大错（Files IV）
Open Threads

maps/Elon-Musk.title: Elon Musk
links: sources/VK科技閱讀時間---拆解-Elon-Musk-六大思考原則
maps/Elon-Musk.content:
Musk 的几条思维模型，以及库里和它们呼应的材料。目前有两个来源：一个是他本人的访谈（一手），一个是台湾读书频道对《馬斯克寶典》的解读（二手）。书本身和 Isaacson 的传记还没有入库。
Core Ideas
按”选问题 → 看清问题 → 下注 → 接收反馈 → 处理冲突”的顺序排列。















































模型一句话笔记一手出处Be Useful有用 = 对每个人有多有用 × 多少人；不要追求荣耀，要追求真功Usefulness is how much you help people times how many people you reachYC 22:33第一性原理用基本组成代替先例：拆到最可能为真的元素，再往上推；配合极限思维First principles reasoning replaces precedent with the constituent elements of a problemYC 25:55白痴指数成品价 ÷ 原料价；比值高，说明钱花在了可以重新设计的过程上The idiot index exposes how much of a price is process inefficiencyYC 27:29 有 1–2% 的数字，没提指数的名字把筹码留在桌上把失败当预期；小机会好过零机会Treating failure as the expected outcome makes a low-probability bet bearableYC 10:09、17:40粉碎 egoego/能力 > 1 会切断和现实的回馈回路，也就是 RL 回路An ego larger than ability cuts the feedback loop with realityYC 23:46不报复你不知道谁将来会救你，不要提早烧桥Not retaliating keeps future options open because you cannot know who will help youIsaacson 传记（二手转述）
这几条之间的关系：

第一性原理算出物理上的成本下限，下限远低于市价，才让”不到 10%“的赌注值得下。
粉碎 ego 和不报复都在处理 ego：前者管怎么接收反馈，后者管怎么处理冲突。
Be Useful 决定往哪里使力，其余几条决定怎么使力。

Related Sources


























来源类型发布时长一句话YC AI Startup School一手访谈2025-0649:41从 Zip2 讲到 2008；有用、粉碎 ego、第一性原理；xAI Colossus；AI 安全靠求真VK：拆解六大思考原则二手解读2026-1019:57读《馬斯克寶典》，用 PayPal 政变和”为什么不报复”串起六条原则
二手说法 vs 一手原话
用 YC 访谈核对 VK 视频里的说法：























































说法（VK 视频）YC 访谈结论ego/能力 > 1 会打破 RL 回路23:46 原话一致，还补充了”内化责任”和”close the loop on reality hard”一致先想去 Netscape 上班，害羞到在大厅里不敢开口07:36 一致一致”我没想造伟大的东西，只想造有用的东西”00:58 一致一致SpaceX、Tesla 成功率不到 10%，“也许是 1%“16:13 一致；访谈里还给了理由：“小机会好过零机会”一致，YC 更完整卖掉 PayPal 后才”把赢来的钱放回桌上”10:09：卖掉 Zip2 时就已经这样做了，2000 万美元几乎全部投进 X.com视频讲得不完整去俄罗斯买 ICBM，回程飞机上用 Excel 算出原料只占 1–2%14:12：俄罗斯人不断加价，让他意识到问题在成本；1–2% 出现在第一性原理那段（27:29），没提飞机和 Excel原料占比一致，飞机上的故事来自书或传记12 月 22 日拿到 NASA 合约，Tesla 平安夜完成融资20:15：大约 12 月 22 日；Tesla 在 12 月 24 日下午 6 点、最后一小时完成融资一致”物理不关心你的感受”10:09 意思相同，说法是”you can’t fool… math and physics are rigorous judges”近似不报复、“因果报应练习”YC 没有提到；网上报道说出自 Isaacson 的传记未核对
库里的呼应

































































Musk库里的材料关系”math and physics are rigorous judges”Naval - It Is Impossible to Fool Mother Nature：“Did your rocket launch?… It is impossible to fool Mother Nature.”几乎是同一句话。Naval 举的例子就是火箭和现实闭环Naval - Free Markets Provide the Best Feedback、Naval - Rational Optimism Is the Way Out（反馈来自自然和市场，不来自同行）同一个判断：要找不会被糊弄的反馈源内化责任Naval - Blame Yourself for Everything, and Preserve Your Agency（文中还说”That’s why Elon goes to Mars”，长远愿景支撑人熬过漫长的时间）为一切负责，才保留了能动性粉碎 egoEgo is friction on execution rather than the source of drive（Naval 说 Elon 不是出于恐惧在做事）Naval 讲 ego 是执行上的摩擦，Musk 讲 ego 会切断反馈，角度互补打破 RL 回路LLMs cannot self-correct without external feedback、RLVR replaces learned reward models with programmatic verifiers这个比喻在 AI 里是字面意思：没有外部验证，就没有有效的学习把失败当预期Fearing failure rejects success because both share one path、Choose problems that are fun whether or not you solve them同样是把”我好不好”和结果脱钩，三者理由不同：反事实、路径、乐趣乐观Naval - Partner With Rational Optimists、Naval - Pessimism Seems Like an Intellectually Serious PositionMusk 的理由是实用的：悲观让人痛苦；Naval 和 Deutsch 的理由是认识论的：问题可解不报复Naval - Play Long-term Games With Long-term People、Naval - Turn Short-Term Games Into Long-Term Games不烧桥，就是让博弈保持为重复博弈第一性原理An experiment chooses between rival explanations、David DeutschDeutsch 反对”从基础推出一切”的基础主义，Musk 的第一性原理更像工程估算。见 Open Threads意识稀有，所以要多行星Naval - Intelligent Species Have Risen Only Once on Planet Earth、Naval - Where Are the Aliens同样从费米悖论出发拆解”不可能”Search and learning are the two methods that scale with arbitrary computationxAI 的做法是把能买到的算力尽快堆起来，这是 bitter lesson 的工程版本
还没入库的出处

The Book of Elon: A Guide to Purpose and Success，Eric Jorgenson 编（他也编了《纳瓦尔宝典》），是 Musk 的语录集。VK 视频的主要依据。
Walter Isaacson《Elon Musk》（2023）。“因果报应练习”、白痴指数的定义、平安夜融资那一幕的出处。
白痴指数在 Starbase 参观里也被提到过（Everyday Astronaut 2021）。这一条还没核实。

Open Threads

第一性原理在 Musk 这里是”拆到最可能为真的元素再往上推”，Deutsch 却认为知识没有坚实的基础，都是猜想。两者是否冲突？可能 Musk 说的”公理”其实是物理定律和价格这类可检验的事实，用法上更接近 Deutsch 说的”好解释”。
“ego/能力 > 1”和 Naval 的”ego 是摩擦”都主张少 ego，但 Musk 本人公开冲突很多。一个人说的方法和他实际的做法，库里应该怎么区分？
不报复只有一个案例，而且从结果倒推。有没有 Musk 选择报复、后来也付出代价的反例？

maps/LLM-Agents.title: LLM Agents
maps/LLM-Agents.content:
LLM agent 的结构、包在模型外面的 harness、一个具体 agent loop（Pi）的实现取舍，以及 Agent Skills。分节沿用 index 的三个主题组：LLM Agent 架构与 harness，Agent loop 工程（Pi），Agent Skills。
Core Ideas
What an agent is

An LLM agent combines planning memory and tool use around a language model core — the language model as the brain, with planning, memory and tool use around it.
An agent’s short-term memory is its context window and long-term memory is external retrieval — in-context learning is bounded by the window; everything else has to be retrieved.
Finite context length forces agent design to work within limited communication bandwidth — the window must hold history, instructions, API context and responses at once.
Tool use is bottlenecked by knowing when and how to call rather than by the tools themselves — the hard part is deciding whether a tool is needed, which one, and with what arguments.
Keep a tool call only when it improves prediction of future tokens — Toolformer keeps a call only if its result lowers the loss on the following tokens.
Self-reflection turns trial and error into within-episode learning — Reflexion-style critique and reset turn failed attempts into iteration inside one episode.
LLMs cannot reliably evaluate their own output in expert domains — in ChemCrow, LLM scoring missed the gap that human experts saw.

The harness around the model

The harness layer around a model matters as much as its raw intelligence — the system that orchestrates planning, tools, context, artifacts and evaluation around the base model.
A harness should keep durable state in files rather than in context — logs, diffs and past trajectories outgrow the window, so keep them on disk.
Context should be maintained as an evolving playbook not an appended log — appending every response grows out of control; curate the context instead.
Code is the universal language for optimizing agent harnesses — a harness is code, so a model that can edit code can search a far larger design space.
Harness edits must be falsifiable and the evaluator must stay outside the loop — bound what the program may edit; keep the verifier, tracer and permissions outside it.
Recursive self-improvement only works above a base-model capability threshold — STOP improved with GPT-4 and degraded with weaker models.
Repeated agent corrections belong in the codebase rather than the conversation — agents copy what is already in the repo, so fix repeated mistakes in code, lint and CI rather than in chat.

Agent loop engineering (Pi)
Structure and state:

A stateless loop core plus a stateful wrapper separates orchestration from session state — the loop takes a context snapshot and a config and remembers nothing between calls.
Inject policy through hooks so the agent loop stays product-agnostic — compaction, permissions, key refresh and shutdown live in config hooks, not in the loop.
Snapshot boundaries between loop and state owner give crash safety for free — the loop works on a shallow copy of messages and tools on each run.
Stream partial messages in place so interrupted contexts stay structurally complete — the partial assistant message holds its slot from the start and is replaced as deltas arrive.

Failure handling:

Agent loops should encode failures as error tool results instead of throwing exceptions — unknown tools, bad arguments and blocked permissions all come back to the model as error results.
Truncated LLM output should fail all tool calls rather than execute salvaged arguments — arguments salvaged from a length-cut response can validate and still be incomplete.
Require all tool results to agree before terminating a batch — the loop stops after a batch only when every result sets the terminate flag.

Agent Skills

Skill descriptions are part of the behavior because they control triggering — the description decides when a skill fires, so tuning it is part of implementation.
Agent skills should be tested like software rather than trusted like prompts — confidence should come from evals, not from the author’s memory that it worked.
Agent skill evals are useful but bounded instruments — evals catch regressions on the cases they encode but cannot by themselves prove broad quality.
Skill evaluations work better in isolated contexts with direct comparisons — clean parallel runs and blinded A/B comparisons give more trustworthy results.
Agent skills need lifecycle management rather than one-time authoring — create, evaluate, compare, re-evaluate and retire.
Capability uplift skills can expire as models absorb their behavior — scaffolds for what the model cannot yet do should be rechecked as models improve.
Encoded preference skills stay valuable when they preserve workflow fidelity — skills that encode a team’s sequence of checks stay useful even with capable models.

Related Sources

Weng - LLM Powered Autonomous Agents
Weng - Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement
Weng - Prompt Engineering
earendil-works - Pi Agent Loop
Anthropic - Improving skill-creator Test, measure, and refine Agent Skills
Lauren Tan - Building a Michelin Kitchen for Agents

Open Threads

Is Pi’s stateless loop core with a stateful wrapper the same idea as keeping durable state in files, at a smaller scale? (lint X5)
Reflexion-style self-reflection helps, yet LLMs cannot self-correct without external feedback: how much of reflection’s gain is really environment feedback? (lint C2)
Lauren Tan ranks Rules and Skills below code and lint as places to put repeated corrections. When is a skill the right home for a correction, and when should it become code? (lint X4)

maps/LLM-Training.title: LLM Training
maps/LLM-Training.content:
模型怎样被训练、怎样被评估、会在哪里出错：推理与 RL 后训练、reward hacking、幻觉、对抗攻击、数据质量，以及视频扩散模型。分节沿用 index 的主题组。Scaling laws 的 6 篇已挂在 Scaling and General Methods，这里不重复列。
Core Ideas
Chain-of-thought and test-time compute

Chain-of-thought lets models allocate variable compute per answer token — a direct answer gets a fixed compute budget; reasoning tokens buy more for harder problems.
Chain-of-thought is not guaranteed to faithfully describe how the model computed its answer — using CoT as interpretability assumes the text matches the computation, which is unproven.
Parallel sampling and sequential revision trade breadth against depth and hard problems need both — best-of-N gives breadth, revision gives depth; hard problems need both.
LLMs cannot self-correct without external feedback — naive self-correction collapses into trivial edits, flips right answers to wrong, and lowers accuracy.

RL with verifiable rewards

Reinforcement learning on automatically verifiable rewards elicits reasoning and emergent reflection — simple policy-gradient RL on checkable answers produces strong reasoning.
RLVR replaces learned reward models with programmatic verifiers — answer checkers, unit tests and format validators take the place of a learned reward model.
Process rewards and tree search failed where simple outcome rewards worked — DeepSeek’s failed attempts: per-step rubrics are hard to define and easier to hack.
GRPO’s biggest gain comes from discarding incorrect samples — most of the gain comes from filtering out wrong samples before the update.
Outcome rewards encourage unfaithful chain-of-thought — rewarding only the answer teaches post-hoc rationalization.
Outcome-only RL imposes a hallucination tax on abstention — answer-only rewards erode the ability to say “I don’t know”.
RL outcomes depend heavily on model priors — the same recipe gives very different results depending on the starting model.
SFT memorizes while RL generalizes — the two pull representations in opposite directions.
Spurious rewards can improve reasoning models by surfacing pretrained capabilities — Qwen models improve even under random rewards; Llama and OLMo do not.
The sharpening versus discovery debate asks whether RL creates or reveals capabilities — does RL post-training create new capabilities or sharpen ones already latent?

Agentic RL

Agentic RL reframes LLMs as policies in POMDPs rather than single-step generators — what separates it from RLHF-style alignment is the horizon.
RL turns agent capabilities from static heuristics into adaptive behavior — across planning, tool use, memory, reasoning, self-improvement and perception.
Self-improvement has three levels from verbal correction to iterative self-training — from critique within one pass to training on the model’s own outputs.
Temporal credit assignment is the bottleneck of long-horizon agentic RL — multi-turn tasks are limited by credit assignment, not by model capability.
Tool use evolves from imitation to outcome-driven RL to long-horizon TIR — ReAct-style imitation, then outcome-driven RL, then long-horizon tool-integrated reasoning.

Reward hacking and evaluation proxies

Every reward function is a hackable proxy for the true goal — agents exploit flaws in the reward to score high without doing the task.
More capable agents exploit reward loopholes more aggressively — higher capability brings higher proxy reward and lower true reward.
RL can turn agents into active reward-hacking exploiters — an RL agent is a goal-seeking exploiter, not a passive victim of prompt injection.
Reward hacking generalizes across tasks but anti-gaming SFT mitigates it — hacking learned in gameable environments carries over to unseen ones.
RLHF makes incorrect answers more convincing to human evaluators — human approval rises without correctness rising.
LLM-as-grader is an imperfect proxy with exploitable biases — LLM judges carry positional and other systematic biases.
Self-refinement feedback loops can hack their own evaluator — when one model generates and evaluates, its score drifts away from the oracle.

Hallucination and fact-checking

Hallucination is either unfaithful to context or ungrounded in world knowledge — in-context hallucination versus extrinsic hallucination.
Fine-tuning LLMs on new knowledge can increase hallucination — new-knowledge examples are learned slowly, and once learned they raise hallucination.
Facts should be verified against retrieved evidence rather than model opinion — in FActScore and SAFE, retrieval-grounded checks beat asking the model.
Attribution turns factuality into a property humans can check — RARR, WebGPT and GopherCite tie claims to sources a person can open.
Inconsistency across samples reveals hallucination with black-box access alone — SelfCheckGPT compares stochastic samples and needs no logprobs.
Verification questions must be answered separately from the draft being checked — CoVe helps only when verification is kept apart from the draft.

Adversarial attacks and safety

Jailbreaks exploit competing objectives and mismatched generalization in safety training — the two ways safety training fails.
Adversarial suffixes transfer from open-source models to commercial APIs — suffixes found on open Vicuna models still jailbreak black-box APIs.
Adversarial attacks trade effectiveness for stealth and fluency — fluent attacks are harder to detect and give up some success rate.
Adversarial robustness is a min-max saddle point problem — find the worst perturbation, then train the model against it.
Adversarial training trades model capability for robustness — the strongest jailbreak defense costs model quality.
Automated red-teaming is bottlenecked by the quality of its harm classifier — every flaw in the classifier becomes an attack pattern for the optimizer.

Data quality and human annotation

A smaller curated dataset can outperform a larger unfiltered one — Stable Video Diffusion’s filtered data beats more raw data.
Unforgettable examples can be pruned without hurting model performance — examples that are never wrong once learned can be dropped.
Training dynamics expose mislabeled data that static filtering misses — mislabels show up in how the model trains on them.
Hard-to-learn samples are often the most informative for OOD generalization — difficulty is a flag for inspection, not a deletion order.
Majority vote assumes equal rater competence so annotators must be weighted by estimated proficiency — equal votes break when spammers join; weight raters by estimated skill.
The median of independent crowd guesses converges to the truth — Galton’s ox: it works only while errors are independent.
Rater disagreement is valid signal in subjective tasks not noise to be eliminated — in subjective tasks, disagreement is data, not measurement error.

Video diffusion models

Extending a pretrained model to a new dimension means inserting identity-initialized modules and freezing the backbone — Make-A-Video, Video LDM and Lumiere add temporal layers to image models.
Temporal mixing layers after shared spatial processing capture sequence coherence better than autoregression — shared spatial layers per frame, then temporal layers that mix across frames.
Generating a whole sequence at once avoids the consistency failures of keyframe-plus-interpolation pipelines — staged keyframe pipelines only see part of the clip at each stage.
Sequence consistency can be enforced at inference time by anchoring attention to a reference frame — Text2Video-Zero turns an image model into a video generator without training.

Related Sources

Weng - Why We Think
Zhang et al - A Survey of RL for Large Reasoning Models
Zhang et al - Landscape of Agentic RL, A Survey
Weng - Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning
Weng - Extrinsic Hallucinations in LLMs
Weng - Adversarial Attacks on LLMs
Weng - Thinking about High-Quality Human Data
Weng - Diffusion Models for Video Generation

Open Threads

Are process rewards easier to hack or more stable? Process rewards and tree search failed where simple outcome rewards worked says hackable, Outcome rewards encourage unfaithful chain-of-thought says stable, and Temporal credit assignment is the bottleneck of long-horizon agentic RL wants dense rewards. Short-answer reasoning and long-horizon agent tasks may need different answers. (lint C1)
Can a model correct itself without outside feedback? CoVe works by taking the draft out of context and Reflexion by using environment feedback; neither is naive self-correction. (lint C2)
SFT memorizes while RL generalizes says SFT is better for new knowledge, while Fine-tuning LLMs on new knowledge can increase hallucination says it raises hallucination. What does adding knowledge by SFT actually cost? (lint C3)
Majority vote over one model’s samples assumes independent errors, but samples from one model are often correlated. When does self-consistency stop helping? See Self-consistency sampling improves reliability through majority vote and The median of independent crowd guesses converges to the truth. (lint C4)

maps/Learning.title: Learning
maps/Learning.content:
Core Ideas

Learning deepens when action creates demand
Curiosity makes it easier to learn from other people
A student mindset makes uncertainty easier to navigate
Specific knowledge is mostly discovered rather than taught
Specific knowledge emerges where capability and authenticity overlap
Specific knowledge often accumulates at the frontier where training is incomplete
Judgment compounds when paired with leverage
Principles become useful only in context
Tools expire, but problems don’t. Every tool is an answer to a question that existed before it did
You don’t learn from the thing working, you learn from the thing not working

Ego is friction on execution rather than the source of drive

Not retaliating keeps future options open because you cannot know who will help you
Self-directed work can dissolve the work-life boundary
Caring too much about the outcome distorts the action
After a mistake realize it correct it learn from it then forgive it

maps/Nassim-Taleb.title: Nassim Taleb
maps/Nassim-Taleb.content:
塔勒布的思维模型，以及库里和它们呼应的材料。目前的来源是正在读的《非对称风险》（Skin in the Game）。Incerto 系列的其他几本还没有入库。
这张地图边读边长：Core Ideas 里”笔记”一列是空的，就表示这个模型还没读到，或者还没提取成笔记。
Core Ideas
按”谁承担后果 → 后果怎样过滤 → 怎样活下来 → 该信谁”的顺序排列。



























































模型一句话笔记出处对称拿好处的人也要承担坏处；风险转移是隐藏的不对称待提取《非对称风险》风险共担即过滤做错要付代价，系统才会学习；学习靠淘汰，不靠个人变聪明Systems learn by removing the parts that fail《非对称风险》Book 1 序言 Part 1（页码待补）少数派主导不肯让步、而且让步成本低的少数，决定多数人的规则待提取《非对称风险》遍历性与破产群体概率不等于时间概率；有破产可能时，期望值就失效了待提取《非对称风险》；Naval 转述理性即生存判断理性看能不能活下来，不看信念对不对待提取《非对称风险》林迪效应时间是唯一可靠的评审待提取《非对称风险》知识分子白痴（IYI）不承担后果的专家，判断会和现实脱节待提取《非对称风险》黑天鹅多少只白天鹅也证明不了天鹅都是白的待提取《黑天鹅》（未入库）；Naval 转述
Related Sources





























来源类型时间一句话Skin in the Game（非对称风险）一手，书2018风险共担、对称、遍历性、少数派主导、林迪效应；正在读Naval：The Beginning of Infinity, Part 1二手转述—Naval 把塔勒布的黑天鹅和 Deutsch 并列，说过去十年只有 Deutsch 和”塔勒布的几本书”让他变聪明了Naval：The Beginning of Infinity, Part 2二手转述—Naval 用塔勒布的遍历性论证批评经济学家：人在定价时算进了破产的风险
Naval 的两段原话：

“Nassim Taleb would go even further and say that they assume false rationality. Humans are pricing in the risk of ruin, the risk of going to zero, and the academics are making mistakes about ergodic reasoning. They’re assuming that what’s good for the ensemble is good for the individual, and it’s not.” — Part 2 全文稿
“One is Nassim Taleb, who popularized the idea of the black swan, which is that no number of white swans disproves the existence of a black swan… All you can do is work with the best explanation you have today.” — Part 1 全文稿

库里的呼应























































塔勒布库里的材料关系风险共担即过滤An ego larger than ability cuts the feedback loop with realityMusk 说的是接收器坏了，塔勒布说的是没有接收器：不承担后果的人根本收不到反馈风险共担即过滤Naval - It Is Impossible to Fool Mother Nature、Naval - Free Markets Provide the Best Feedback反馈要来自自然和市场，不能来自同行风险共担即过滤LLMs cannot self-correct without external feedback、Self-refinement feedback loops can hack their own evaluator、RLVR replaces learned reward models with programmatic verifiers在 AI 里，打分的必须是和结果绑定的外部检验器风险共担即过滤Explanatory creativity can cross gaps that evolution cannot、Preserving the means of error correction is the heart of morality塔勒布：系统靠剔除承载错误的人来学习；Deutsch：解释让想法替人去死，系统更该保住的是纠错手段对称Every reward function is a hackable proxy for the true goal代理人和委托人的利益不一致，就会去钻指标的空子遍历性与破产Treating failure as the expected outcome makes a low-probability bet bearableMusk 下的低概率赌注不会让他破产吗？对照塔勒布，见 Open Threads林迪效应、长期Honesty pays in long games because duplicity gets more expensive as information flows、Naval - Play Long-term Games With Long-term People重复博弈里，活下来的策略才是好策略黑天鹅David Deutsch、An experiment chooses between rival explanations两人都反对归纳法，但理由不同，见 Open Threads付出真实代价drafts/虚实之间：“一切理论都是灰色的，直到你将他们用于真实的选择、付出真实的代价。“几乎就是 skin in the game 的定义

Core Ideas

APO 的核心落地建议
Prompt optimization turns prompt writing into measurable search
APO systems share a five-stage optimization anatomy
APO quality depends on validation data and metric design
Prompt optimization spaces can be discrete continuous or hybrid
Few-shot prompt performance swings wildly with example choice and order
Chain-of-thought pays off only for complex reasoning in large models
Prompt explanations fail by being nonfactual rather than inconsistent
Self-consistency sampling improves reliability through majority vote

Foundational Methods

Automatic prompt engineering treats instructions as programs
Textual gradients make prompt errors editable in natural language
Seedless prompt induction lowers entry cost but still needs task examples

Reading Order

maps/Scaling-and-General-Methods.title: Scaling and General Methods
maps/Scaling-and-General-Methods.content:
Core Ideas
The bitter lesson

General methods that keep scaling with computation beat human-knowledge methods in the long run — methods that keep improving as compute grows win; it is about algorithms that scale, not scale alone.
Built-in human knowledge helps in the short term and then plateaus — domain knowledge gives quick gains, then caps what extra compute can buy.
Search and learning are the two methods that scale with arbitrary computation — the two classes of technique that turn more compute directly into capability.
AI should be built to discover rather than to contain what we have discovered — build in meta-methods that find complexity, not our own discoveries.
Researchers resist the bitter lesson because building in knowledge is satisfying and pays off early — why the field keeps repeating the mistake.
Reasoning RL learns search inside the model instead of running it outside — in reasoning RL, hand-designed search lost; search moved inside the model and human structure moved into the verifier.

How performance scales with compute

Under a fixed compute budget, model size and training tokens should scale together — Chinchilla: split a fixed budget evenly between parameters and tokens.
The Kaplan-Chinchilla exponent gap dissolves as scale grows — the optimal exponent is local and converges as scale grows.
The power-law exponent is a property of the problem not the architecture — architecture shifts the intercept, the slope belongs to the task.
Scaling-law predictions are fragile to trivial fitting choices — extrapolated predictions depend on the fitting procedure.

What the compute is spent on

Data quality can change compute efficiency more than token count — same token count, very different compute efficiency.
Repeated tokens decay in value and larger models overfit them faster — when unique data runs out, repeats lose value.

Related Sources

Rich Sutton - The Bitter Lesson
Stanford CS336 - Lecture 01 - Overview, Tokenization
Weng - Scaling Laws, Carefully

Open Threads

The bitter lesson says to build in only what scales, yet data curation clearly changes compute efficiency: where does human-supplied structure stop being a crutch and start being a lever?
How do the lesson’s favored methods, search and learning, show up in current reasoning RL? Partly answered in Reasoning RL learns search inside the model instead of running it outside: supplying verifiability is a lever, supplying solution steps is a crutch.
Does RL discover or only sharpen? If it mostly sharpens, pretraining is where discovery happens: see The sharpening versus discovery debate asks whether RL creates or reveals capabilities.

maps/张一鸣.content:
张一鸣的几条思维模型，以及库里和它们呼应的材料。目前有三个来源，正好隔了十年：2010 年前后的微博（网友摘录，二手），2021 年的 9 周年演讲和卸任 CEO 全员信（本人，一手）。这张图最有意思的不是单条观点，而是同一个人从”克己”走到”平常心”的变化，见”十年前后”一节。

notes/A-CEO-at-the-center-of-a-growing-o.title: A CEO at the center of a growing organization drifts into an internal view
notes/A-CEO-at-the-center-of-a-growing-o.content:
EN — Zhang Yiming names a “negative scale effect” for CEOs: as the business and organization grow, the CEO becomes the central node, spends each day hearing reports, approving and deciding, and slides into an internal perspective while their knowledge stops updating. He had told other founders this three years earlier, and in his 2021 letter stepping down as CEO he applied it to himself: before 2017 he still followed new work in machine learning, but in the last three years he had barely learned, his saved articles and videos read in fragments, and he could no longer keep up in technical discussions. He judged that he had been “living off old capital” and that his annual OKRs were only linear extensions. His remedy was structural, not more effort: hand daily management to Liang Rubo and spend a decade on learning, systematic thinking and hands-on trying. He described himself as preferring “to study the principles of organizations and markets in order to reduce management”. Caveat: this is the official, self-authored account of a leadership change; other reasons (regulatory and geopolitical pressure in 2020–21 were widely discussed) are not in the letter, and the vault has no independent source to weigh them.
中文 — 张一鸣提出过 CEO 的”负规模效应”：业务和组织变大以后，CEO 成了中心节点，每天听汇报、做审批和决策，容易陷入内部视角，知识结构更新缓慢。三年前他把这条讲给创业者听，2021 年卸任 CEO 的全员信里，他把它用在了自己身上：17 年之前他还能关注机器学习的新进展，近三年已经没有太多学习，收藏的专业视频和文章断断续续地读，在技术讨论会上也难以跟上。他的判断是过去几年”很大程度都在吃老本”，年度 OKR 只是线性延伸。他的办法是改结构而不是更努力：把日常管理交给梁汝波，自己以十年为期专注学习、系统思考、动手尝试。他对自己的描述是”更喜欢研究组织和市场原理来减少管理”。局限： 这是一次人事变动的官方、本人署名的说法；当时外界广泛讨论的其他原因（2020–21 年的监管和地缘压力）不在信里，库里也没有独立来源可以对照。
Key Quotes

「CEO 要避免一个普遍的负规模效应——当业务和组织变复杂规模变大的时候，作为中心节点的 CEO 容易陷入被动：每天要听很多汇报总结，做很多审批和决策，容易导致内部视角，知识结构更新缓慢。」
「我感觉过去几年很大程度都在”吃老本”。」
「我不是传统意义上的成熟管理者，我也不是很擅长社交，我更喜欢研究组织和市场原理来减少管理，喜欢自己上网、看书、听歌、发呆。」

notes/A-bug-you-can-reproduce-on-demand-.filePath: notes/A bug you can reproduce on demand is already 90% fixed. Everything before that point is guesswork and guessing scales terribly.md
notes/A-bug-you-can-reproduce-on-demand-.title: A bug you can reproduce on demand is already 90% fixed. Everything before that point is guesswork and guessing scales terribly
notes/A-bug-you-can-reproduce-on-demand-.content:
Debugging is mostly the work of getting to a reliable reproduction. Before that point it’s guesswork, and guesswork scales terribly: change a line, refresh, add console.log after console.log until eleven of them print and you can’t tell them apart. The Coding Gopher calls that “not debugging, that’s a seance.”
His three steps start with not touching the code. First, hypothesize: state specifically what is failing (“we invalidate the cache before the write commits, so a concurrent read repopulates it with the old value”), not “the data is wrong.” A hypothesis is useful because it can be wrong. Second, isolate: strip away everything that isn’t the bug until you have the smallest failing case; most bugs are found here. Third, write the failing test. Once it reproduces reliably the fix is usually trivial, and the test stays forever.
He also says to learn a real debugger: a conditional breakpoint (“pause here, but only when user ID is null”) replaces a hundred print statements.
This is An experiment chooses between rival explanations at desk scale. A specific hypothesis gives the reproduction something to decide, and the failing test is the experiment.
Caveat: some bugs resist reproduction: races, load-dependent failures, production-only data. There the work shifts to logging and observability, which are reproduction in slow motion. “90% fixed” is a rhetorical number, not a measurement.
Key Quotes

“A bug you can reproduce on demand is already 90% fixed. Everything before that point is guesswork and guessing scales terribly.” (03:50)
“A hypothesis is something you can be wrong about, which is what makes it useful.” (04:28)

Related:

An experiment chooses between rival explanations — a reproduction decides between hypotheses
Effective AI coding treats output as hypotheses to be validated rather than code to review — the same habit applied to generated code: the test is what accepts or rejects it
Every bug anyone hit before you is sitting in the history, and a lot of people don’t know how to query it — once you have a reproduction, bisect can find the commit

notes/A-harness-should-keep-durable-stat.title: A harness should keep durable state in files rather than in context
notes/A-harness-should-keep-durable-stat.content:
EN — In long-horizon agent runs, artifacts such as experiment logs, code diffs, error traces, and past trajectories quickly outgrow the context window, so a harness should keep durable state in the file system and let the model read, write, and edit files via shell commands instead of carrying the whole workflow in context. The same principle makes subagent parallelism recoverable: outputs stored as files, logs, and status records survive interruptions and can be reasoned over later, while outputs that live only in transient chat context quickly become obsolete and hidden.
中文 — 在长程 agent 运行中，实验日志、代码 diff、错误追踪和过往轨迹等产物很快会超出上下文窗口，因此 harness 应把持久状态保存在文件系统中，让模型通过 shell 命令读写编辑文件，而不是把整个工作流塞进上下文。同样的原则使子 agent 并行可恢复：以文件、日志和状态记录存储的输出能在中断后幸存并供日后推理，而只存在于临时聊天上下文中的输出很快就会过时并被埋没。

notes/A-smaller-curated-dataset-can-outp.title: A smaller curated dataset can outperform a larger unfiltered one
notes/A-smaller-curated-dataset-can-outp.content:
EN — Stable Video Diffusion reports that filtering video data — removing clips with little motion (low optical flow), excessive on-screen text (OCR), or low aesthetic and text-image similarity scores — produced better models even though the resulting dataset was much smaller. Data quality acts as a bottleneck on model quality, so curation is a first-class lever alongside scale, not a cosmetic preprocessing step.
中文 — Stable Video Diffusion 报告称，过滤视频数据——移除运动过少（低光流）、屏幕文字过多（OCR）或美学与文图相似度分数低的片段——得到的模型更好，即使数据集因此小得多。数据质量是模型质量的瓶颈，因此筛选与规模一样是一等杠杆，而非装点门面的预处理步骤。

notes/A-stateless-loop-core-plus-a-state.title: A stateless loop core plus a stateful wrapper separates orchestration from session state
notes/A-stateless-loop-core-plus-a-state.content:
Pi’s agent loop is a stateless function: it receives a context snapshot and a config, emits events, and returns new messages without remembering anything between calls. A separate Agent class owns the transcript, steering queues, and lifecycle, passing snapshots in and committing only completed messages out. The split makes the orchestration logic independently testable — tests drive it directly with a mock stream function — while stateful concerns like interruption and cancellation live in the wrapper.

notes/A-working-implementation-now-signa.filePath: notes/A working implementation now signals twenty percent done rather than eighty percent.md
notes/A-working-implementation-now-signa.title: A working implementation now signals twenty percent done rather than eighty percent
notes/A-working-implementation-now-signa.content:
When code was written by hand, reaching a working implementation meant a task was roughly 80% complete. With LLM-generated drafts, a working implementation feels more like 20% done. The model reliably produces code that meets explicit, verifiable criteria, but the remaining work — restructuring for maintainability, judging whether the shape is right, deciding what belongs and what is extraneous — is exactly the part LLMs cannot yet predict well. The effort therefore shifts from producing a working version to iterating heavily on structure afterward, and this iteration is consistently underestimated.
Supporting Ideas

LLM coding usefulness came from crossing a reliability threshold, not raw capability
LLM-generated code is locally functional but globally incoherent
Effective AI coding treats output as hypotheses to be validated rather than code to review
Fearing failure rejects success because both share one path — same structure in another domain: a visible milestone (working code) is the overrated 20%, and the real payoff is in the iteration after it.

notes/AI-coding-tools-create-a-K-shaped-.title: AI coding tools create a K-shaped workforce split between augmented engineers and those unable to leverage them
notes/AI-coding-tools-create-a-K-shaped-.content:
AI coding tools amplify existing skill differentials rather than flattening them. Engineers who can guide, review, and validate AI output see 10% to multi-fold productivity gains, while those who cannot leverage the tools well see marginal or even detrimental results. The learning curve and the need for rigorous line-by-line review mean the tools reward curiosity and foundational competence rather than replacing it. This creates a K-shaped divergence: one branch rises with augmented leverage, the other falls behind as routine coding gets commoditized.

notes/AI-productivity-claims-conflict-be.filePath: notes/AI productivity claims conflict between anecdotal reports and formal studies.md
notes/AI-productivity-claims-conflict-be.title: AI productivity claims conflict between anecdotal reports and formal studies
notes/AI-productivity-claims-conflict-be.content:
Anecdotal reports of 10x productivity gains from AI coding tools conflict sharply with formal studies that show minimal or no measurable gains. Part of the gap is methodological: many formal studies predate modern RLHF models and use weaker baselines. Another part is that gains are highly uneven — they depend on the user’s skill, the task type, and the workflow. Self-reported productivity is also vulnerable to confirmation bias and the difficulty of measuring what “productivity” means across code quality, maintenance, and throughput. The truth is likely that gains are real for some users on some tasks, but far from universal or uniform.
