sources/Elon-Musk---Digital-Superintelli.content:
Summary
Y Combinator AI Startup School 上的一场访谈。主持人是 YC 的人，现场观众是 18–25 岁的工程师和创业者。前半场 Musk 讲自己从 Zip2 到 2008 年的经历，以及给年轻人的建议：有用、粉碎 ego、第一性原理；后半场讲 xAI 的 Colossus 集群、合成数据、人形机器人、多行星、Neuralink 和 AI 安全。《馬斯克寶典》里有好几段原话出自这场访谈，所以它是 VK科技閱讀時間 - 拆解 Elon Musk 六大思考原則 的一手出处，可以用来核对视频里转述的内容。

时长：49:41，英文

Key Takeaways
本想造有用的东西，不是伟大的东西（00:58）
“I didn’t originally think I would build something great. I wanted to try to build something useful.” 他当时觉得成功的概率不高，但想至少试一试。
先求职，不是先创业（02:02–08:07）
1995 年他向 Stanford 材料科学博士项目申请延期一个季度，“因为这很可能会失败，然后我得回来”。他投简历给 Netscape，没有回音，在大厅里转悠，但太害羞，不敢跟人搭话，于是自己写软件。“既然在互联网公司找不到工作，我只好开一家互联网公司。“他们睡在办公室，在 YMCA 洗澡。
数学和物理是严格的裁判（10:09）
造火箭、造车、写能稳定运行的软件，都必须”最大程度地求真”，否则东西就不能用。“you can’t fool… math and physics are rigorous judges.” 他拿这一点和政治里极低的信噪比作对比。
把筹码留在桌上，从 Zip2 就开始了（10:09–12:10）
Zip2 让他分到 2000 万美元，他几乎全部投进 X.com，“I kept the chips on the table”。卖掉 PayPal 之后，他在 NASA 网站上找不到载人登火星的日期，最初的想法是做一个慈善项目：把温室送上火星。2001–2002 年他去俄罗斯买 ICBM，对方不断加价，他由此意识到，问题不是缺少意愿，而是成本。
小机会好过零机会（16:13–18:14）
他估计 SpaceX 的成功率”less than 10%… maybe 1%“。理由是：大型国防承包商不会去推进火箭技术，“所以它要么来自一家创业公司，要么根本不会发生。小机会好过零机会”。招人时他直接说”我们很可能会死”。当上首席工程师，是因为请不到好的人选。前三次发射失败，如果第四次也失败，钱就花光了。
2008 年最后十天（18:14–22:16）
NASA 的补给合约大约在 12 月 22 日拿到，他脱口而出”I love you guys”。Tesla 的融资在 12 月 24 日下午 6 点完成，那是最后一天的最后一小时；再晚两天，圣诞节后就发不出工资了。
有用 = 有用程度 × 人数（22:16）
“try to be as useful as possible”：总效用曲线下的面积，就是你对别人有多有用乘以多少人，“almost like the physics definition of true work”。“don’t aspire to glory, aspire to work.” 判断标准是：如果这东西成功了，会对多少人有多有用？
ego 与能力之比（23:46–24:49）
“always be smashing your ego… internalize responsibility… a major failure mode is when ego to ability ratio is greater than one… you’re going to basically break the feedback loop to reality, and in AI terms you’ll break your RL loop.” 要保持强的 RL 回路，就要内化责任、把 ego 降到最低，不论任务宏大还是卑微都去做。所以他偏爱”engineering”而不是”research”，也不想把 xAI 叫做”lab”，因为用最朴素、ego 最低的词往往是对的。“close the loop on reality hard.”
第一性原理与极限思维（24:49–30:19）
第一性原理就是”把事物拆到最可能为真的基本公理元素，再尽可能严密地往上推”，而不是靠类比推理。另一个工具是”thinking in the limit”：把某个量推到最小或最大，看会发生什么。火箭的例子：常规做法是看历史上火箭卖多少钱；第一性原理的做法是看火箭由哪些材料组成、各重多少、每公斤多少钱，这就给出了成本的下限。原料只占历史成本的 1–2%，所以制造一定非常低效，而这还没算可复用。xAI 的例子：供应商说 10 万张 H100 要 18–24 个月，他把需求拆成厂房、电力、冷却、电力平滑、组网几项，逐项去解决（Memphis 的旧 Electrolux 工厂、租来的发电机、美国约四分之一的移动冷却设备、Megapack），他自己也睡在机房里布线。
AI 的部分（30:19–49:41）

人类生成的高质量预训练数据快用完了，合成数据的难点在于判断它是否”grounded in reality”。
物理教科书对推理训练有用。
人形机器人数量会是人的 5–10 倍。
他认可 Hinton 的说法：AI 导致人类毁灭的概率约 10–20%。
AI 安全最重要的是”rigorous adherence to truth”，强迫 AI 相信不真实的东西是危险的。
关于多行星：用费米悖论论证意识可能极其稀有，“tiny candle in a vast darkness”。

Extracted Notes

Usefulness is how much you help people times how many people you reach
First principles reasoning replaces precedent with the constituent elements of a problem
补充为一手出处：An ego larger than ability cuts the feedback loop with reality、Treating failure as the expected outcome makes a low-probability bet bearable、The idiot index exposes how much of a price is process inefficiency

Related

人物地图：Elon Musk
“can’t fool math and physics” 和 Naval - It Is Impossible to Fool Mother Nature 几乎是同一句话。
意识稀有、需要多行星来保护，可以对照 Naval - Intelligent Species Have Risen Only Once on Planet Earth 和 Naval - Where Are the Aliens。

sources/Hacker-News---We-might-all-be-AI.title: We might all be AI engineers now
sources/Hacker-News---We-might-all-be-AI.content:
Summary
A Hacker News discussion debating the impact of LLM coding tools on software engineering. The conversation splits into two broad camps: proponents who describe the tools as supercharged code search and autocomplete delivering 10% to multi-fold productivity gains, and skeptics who argue LLM code is locally passable but globally incoherent, prone to hidden technical debt and security flaws. The discussion also covers the K-shaped workforce split, the cognitive load of reviewing AI output, the redefinition of engineering skills, and broader societal concerns about labor displacement and corporate control of AI tooling.
Key Takeaways

AI coding tools create a K-shaped workforce split between skilled augmented engineers and those unable to leverage them well.
LLM-generated code is locally functional but globally incoherent, tending to produce hidden technical debt that is hard to debug.
Effective AI coding shifts the workflow toward treating output as hypotheses to be validated through tests and specs, not code to be passively reviewed.
The cognitive load of reviewing AI output is real and qualitatively different from writing code yourself, contributing to burnout.
Anecdotal productivity claims conflict sharply with formal studies that show minimal measurable gains, partly because many studies predate modern RLHF models.
Traditional engineering skills are being redefined rather than obviated — judgment, specification, and verification become the core value.
Spec-driven development is rising as AI shifts coding toward writing clear, unambiguous requirements and formal specs.

Detailed Discussion Breakdown
Theme 1: AI Productivity Claims, Measurement & Workflow Shifts

noemit: AI quietly writes strong code most of the time; people only share failures. Works with global engineers of varied skill; CA startup engineers see ~10x gains. Skilled guidance is required, creating a K-shaped workforce. (Pro-AI)
bryanrasmussen: Questions how pro-AI users report productivity gains despite third-party HN-posted studies showing no measurable gains. Later asks about ticket structuring for successful AI workflows. (Skeptical, evidence-seeking)
peteforde: Frustrated by demands to quantify obvious gains. Uses Opus 4.5 via Cursor ($200/month base + $50-100 overages; peak $700/month). Calls less powerful models produce bad results skeptics generalize. AI is cheaper than unreliable human hires — LLM $3600/year vs. hiring. (Strongly Pro-AI)
remus: Compares AI productivity studies to flawed power tool vs. hand tool studies; a chainsaw user would laugh at claims of no gains. (Pro-AI)
KronisLV: Sees 3-5x personal gains using Claude Code + $100/month Opus 4.6 Max. Notes 80% of devs may see marginal or detrimental gains due to learning curve. Previously used Cerebras Code but GLM 4.7 needed frequent fixes. (Pro-AI with caveats)
prescriptivist (principal engineer, 10yrs same codebases): Increased inbound volume handled faster; first time chipping away at “nice-to-have” backlog. SEV rates unchanged; code review volume near breaking point. 20% of work inbound throughput increase. (Pro-AI)
overgard: Personal 10-20% gains; uses AI for repetitive React form code; uses as rubber duck for idea bouncing. Data editor project generating many repetitive fields. (Mixed, daily user, moderate gains, anti-hype)
sameerds: AI acts as supercharged code search/autocomplete; saved 1 week finding rare complex component changes; acts only as reviewer. (Pro-AI)
SquibblesRedux: Defines LLMs as supercharged search + autocomplete + adjustable randomness. (Neutral/Pro-AI)
_zagj: Most productivity studies predate modern RLHF models; 10x claims unfounded; AI is only improving. (Mixed, pro-adoption, anti-hype)
codebolt: Effective prompting requires formal, detailed specs (“formal letter to British throne” level clarity); many devs lack this writing skill. Contrasts old Google keyword-search habit. (Pro-AI, workflow skill shift)
pragma_x: Unambiguous specs + jargon/CS formalisms/patterns prevent LLM “creativity”; coding now equals robust requirements doc writing. Compares unwanted AI creativity to unwanted intern creativity. (Pro-AI)
ValentineC: Spec-driven development rising; devs use AI to write prompts for other AI to write code. (Neutral/Pro-AI)
sdf2df (CEO): Revamped hiring to test thinking, not coding. Personal Grok video project produced good output but was extremely painful and costly (50 free Grok accounts, tens of thousands in implied costs); preferred humans. (Mixed, pro-thinking hiring, skeptical of production LLM use)

Theme 2: AI Code Quality, Architecture & “Hallucinations”

overgard: AI code locally functional, globally incoherent; happily generates architecturally bad code; LLMs perform worse as codebases grow; AGENTS.md worsens outcomes. (Skeptical of unguided AI)
jihadjihad: Proposes agent context rule: changes at layer N require consideration of layers N-1 (dependencies) and N+1 (consumers), analogous to grep -A/-B context flags. Untested proposal. (Mixed, identifies problem, proposes untested fix)
archagon: AI code will create “future full of horrifying security holes, heisenbugs”; agentic programming is management of non-improving workers; models owned by “authoritarian, billionaire, misanthropic cultists”. Warns of $20/month subscription price jumping 10x on market capture. (Strongly Skeptical)
_dwt: Identifies “hallucination-adjacent” issues: incorrect numerical algorithm parameters, failed fix loops from missed steps, subtle domain-specific algorithm choices. Personal experience with typed/tested code with no non-existent function calls, but other subtle errors. (Skeptical)
johnfn: “Hallucinations are irrelevant in practice; learn AI’s weak domains and avoid them.” Compares complaining about hallucinations to using a hammer on screws and blaming the tool. Cites typical HN skeptic absurd claims (GPT 3.5 = Opus 4.6 interchangeable, attacks on engineering ability). (Pro-AI)
choutos: Reframe AI output as hypothesis, not code to review; shift workflow to tests/validation/specs; deliverable is proof of correctness, not code. Teams making this explicit shift adapt best. (Pro-AI with workflow adjustment)
scott_s: AI effectively makes everyone tech leads; review/validation role is not new. (Neutral/Pro-AI)
kif: LLMs excel at prototyping/boilerplate; Claude’s mistakes are non-negligible; dual coding+review role causes burnout/higher cognitive load for self and colleagues. (Mixed)
sn0wflak3s (article submitter): Cognitive load of reviewing AI output is real and different from writing code; reviews every AI-generated line non-negotiably; improves with tighter feedback loops/testing. (Mixed, pro-AI with caveats)
kdheiwns: Engineers fix problems when noticed; AI “sends happy little emoji while it continues to trash your codebase” to total unmaintainability. (Skeptical)
skydhash: Quotes Dijkstra (EWD249, EWD667) to note clear thought/structured complexity is always essential engineering skill. (Neutral/Pro-clear-thinking)
godelski: Quotes Dijkstra (EWD288) to note “program correctness concern repulsive to many programmers”; LLMs double down on “it works therefore it’s correct” mindset. (Skeptical)
Anamon: AI increases superficial short-term productivity but may cause extreme technical debt wiping long-term gains. (Skeptical)
wk320189: Dismisses tern’s points as “standard AI promotion talking points”; demands proof of working code. (Skeptical)

Theme 3: Skill Obsolescence, Labor & Historical Analogies

prescriptivist: Traditional engineering skills are “more or less obviated now”; genie out of bottle, no labor movement/deus ex machina reversal. (Pro-AI, resigned to change)
lll-o-lll: Compares current moment to 19th-century British textile weavers (Luddites). Acknowledges AI output inferior but irrelevant; governments will not protect skilled workers; all factory-processable work at risk. Not hopeful for better societal outcomes. (Skeptical/negative acceptance)
dasil003: Software already automates manual work + simpler programs; LLM is a large non-deterministic, leaky abstraction hop; traditional manual coders “cooked”; adapting to LLM tooling offers bright future. (Pro-AI, adaptation message)
archagon: Rejects obsoletion claims; LLMs not intelligent, limited by training corpus; craft undervalued by pro-AI folks eager to be PMs; not beholden to “AI-pilled corporation” salary. Mitch Hedberg cook/farm analogy for agentic programming critique. (Strongly Skeptical)
bandrami: Never had to learn JavaScript 20 years ago or blockchains 5 years ago; still uses Perl; does not have to learn AI agents. Companies more hesitant to adopt AI than individual devs due to legal/TCO concerns. (Skeptical of inevitability)
KronisLV: Not learning AI practicalities makes developers less competitive; corporations do not care about AI flaws; compares to JavaScript learning enabling 5-10 years of paid work. (Pro-AI, market pressure argument)
norir: Claims AI can write code equal in quality to manually typed code only applies to the claimant personally. (Skeptical)
thunky: Some programmers see too much value in their own work; obsolescence is not punishment. (Neutral/Skeptical of craftsmanship sanctity)
overgard (response to thunky): Calling craftsmanship obsolete equals punishing care and quality. (Skeptical)
Anamon: Models utterly fail outside training corpus space; 2022 software would be peak capability if progress stops; security/reliability progress reversed entirely. (Strongly Skeptical)

Theme 4: Societal, Ethical & Political Concerns

_dwt: Rejects AI inevitability; humanity can choose not to deploy transformative tech (nuclear weapons used twice only); CEOs calling LLMs bigger than fire/nukes are “psychopathic”; public widely distrusts AI; pushes for data royalties/planetary sovereign wealth fund. Cites supersonic airliners, eugenics, Betamax as examples of world-changing tech not widely adopted. (Strongly Skeptical)
prescriptivist: Agrees humanity could stop AI but capital is too powerful; business pays bills/healthcare; larger revolution against capital only solution; acknowledges participation may seed end of own career. (Pro-AI, resigned to capital pressure)
solaire_oa: Recommends local LLMs (llama.cpp) to democratize AI; removes reliance on centralized providers; hedges against provider investment unsustainability. (Mixed, pro-AI with local deployment)
overgard: Trillions poured into barely-understood tech for awful economic revolution not inevitable; need non-idiot leaders; normies waking up to issues; need working SEC to punish grifting CEOs manipulating markets with fear. (Strongly Skeptical)
palmotea: AI dumped into 2026 extractive shareholder economy; AI designed to eliminate well-compensated knowledge workers; few workers running hot burning out with mass idle low-wage replacements. (Strongly Skeptical)
salawat: Criticizes tern’s “taste” claim as armchair theorizing; capitalism’s optimization function is capital allocation, not craftsmanship. (Skeptical)
godelski (AI researcher): LLMs trained for human preference/accuracy/natural speech maximizes their ability to deceive humans; warns against self-delusion of being uniquely unaffected. (Skeptical)
bluefirebrand: Suggests pro-AI commentators may have financial investments in AI companies or blog traffic incentives to hype tech. (Skeptical)
sd9: Calls wartywhoa23’s “wannabe systems engineer” jab unnecessarily antagonistic. (Neutral, civility call)

Theme 5: Learning, Knowledge & Non-Traditional Engineer Access

tern (art degree, CS dropout, 15yr HN hobbyist): AI removes hands/eyes/tokens as bottleneck; now only bottleneck is ideas. Building complex custom PL/bytecode/runtime with formal specs, algebraic topology, obscure PL concepts. Notes heavy chatbot reading is making own writing style chatbot-like; plans 19th-century literature reading fix. (Pro-AI)
godelski: Disagrees LLMs are effective learning tools; “swiss cheese knowledge” from skipping textbook/prose learning; same mechanism causes conspiracy theories; textbooks converged to current structure for good reason. Complexity (computational + conceptual) is real bottleneck, not hands/ideas. (Skeptical of LLM learning)
samiv: AI draws lazy non-learners; like skipping to math book answers; global school LLM cheating crises. (Skeptical)
johnfn: More to learn now than ever pre-AI; spends more time learning previously out-of-reach topics. (Pro-AI)
overgard: Happy for tern’s empowerment, compares to early PHP web dev era; irritated by “everyone must do AI” hype train causing culture shift harm analogous to crypto damage. (Mixed, supports individual use, anti-hype)
beepbooptheory: No need for AI tools; faster, smarter, synthesizes disparate SoT model-impossible concepts; will thrive when others forget how to read; will remain “zen and unburdened” in emacs. (Strongly Skeptical)
distrill: AI hesitation is not a fringe position; defensive line-drawing comes off as uncurious. (Pro-AI)
godelski (broader discourse): Essential engineer skill is asking “what do they see that I don’t” across all debates; differing unstated assumptions drive most disagreements; LLM smooth jargon makes truth distinction harder. (Neutral, mutual understanding advocate)
peteforde: Warns against artificial AI critic/user divisions; we’re all same camp; tech adoption moves like time’s arrow; geeks are just geeks. (Pro-AI, unity advocate)
doug_durham: Old manual coding was not perfect; humans make frequent stupid code mistakes; LLM mistake fear is unreasonable objection. (Pro-AI)
axus: Parent’s “curious” framing applies to AI users only (curious users self-improve, incurious want money/software without caring how made); objects to VC bubble company means of production centralization. (Skeptical)

Extracted Notes

AI coding tools create a K-shaped workforce split between augmented engineers and those unable to leverage them
LLM-generated code is locally functional but globally incoherent
Effective AI coding treats output as hypotheses to be validated rather than code to review
The cognitive load of reviewing AI output is real and different from writing code
AI productivity claims conflict between anecdotal reports and formal studies
Specific knowledge becomes more valuable as AI commoditizes routine coding
Spec-driven development is rising as AI shifts coding toward writing clear requirements

sources/Ivan-Zhao---Steam,-Steel,-and-In.title: Steam, Steel, and Infinite Minds
sources/Ivan-Zhao---Steam,-Steel,-and-In.content:
Summary
Ivan Zhao argues that AI should be understood not as a better search box but as a new industrial material for knowledge work. The article frames AI agents as “infinite minds” that can reshape work at three levels: the individual worker, the organization, and the wider economy.
Key Takeaways

New technologies are often first understood through old metaphors, which delays redesign.
Knowledge work is harder to automate than coding because its context is fragmented and its outputs are less verifiable.
Humans should supervise AI from leveraged positions rather than remain inside every loop.
AI could let organizations scale without relying on human communication as the main load-bearing structure.
Current AI adoption mostly bolts chatbots onto old workflows instead of redesigning around new constraints.
At economic scale, AI may make organizations faster, less legible, and far larger, much like industrial infrastructure changed cities.

Extracted Notes

AI knowledge work improves when context is consolidated
Humans should supervise AI from leveraged positions rather than sit inside every loop
Organizations can use AI as a load-bearing context layer
Most AI adoption still imitates old tools instead of redesigning workflows
New infrastructure changes scale before it changes culture
AI-native knowledge work is a verification problem before it is an intelligence problem

sources/Jacob-O'Bryant---2x,-not-10x---C.filePath: sources/Jacob O'Bryant - 2x, not 10x - Coding with LLMs in 2026.md
sources/Jacob-O'Bryant---2x,-not-10x---C.title: 2x, not 10x: coding with LLMs in 2026
sources/Jacob-O'Bryant---2x,-not-10x---C.content:
Summary
A short essay arguing that LLMs’ surge in coding adoption during 2026 came not from raw intelligence gains but from crossing a reliability threshold: they became dependable enough to run inside automated feedback loops. The author proposes a “staircase hypothesis” — being tall enough to climb one step at a time is what matters; being tall enough to take two or three at once matters much less. On this view, further model improvements alone will yield diminishing productivity returns, and most future gains will come from the industry retooling around the capabilities that already exist rather than from smarter models.
Key Takeaways

LLMs became useful for coding because they can iterate reliably toward explicit, objectively verifiable acceptance criteria (“make a button that does X, then click it and confirm it does X”).
The “staircase hypothesis”: once models are reliable enough to run in automated feedback loops, further capability gains have sharply diminishing impact on productivity — climbing a taller staircase is not the same skill as swimming.
LLMs are strong at producing rough drafts against explicit criteria but weak at judgment questions like “is there a more maintainable structure?” or “does this doc include the right information and omit the extraneous?”
A working implementation used to mean a task was ~80% done; with LLM drafts it now feels ~20% done, because the heavy iteration on structure comes after.
Telling the model “never write READMEs, docstrings, or comments — I will write those myself later” markedly improves output quality.
The realistic near-term gain is roughly 2x, not 10x; getting to 10x would require routing around LLMs’ fundamental weaknesses (better tooling, sandboxes, spec-driven workflows, possibly viable vibe coding), not just better models.

Extracted Notes

LLM coding usefulness came from crossing a reliability threshold, not raw capability
A working implementation now signals twenty percent done rather than eighty percent
Near-term AI productivity gains come from retooling the industry rather than better models

sources/LLM-Wiki-中文版.title: LLM Wiki（中译）
sources/LLM-Wiki-中文版.content:
一种使用 LLM 构建个人知识库的模式。

原文：gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f
作者：Andrej Karpathy

这是一个”想法文件”，设计目的是让你复制粘贴给自己的 LLM Agent（例如 OpenAI Codex、Claude Code、OpenCode / Pi 等）。它的目标是传达高层思路，具体细节由你的 Agent 与你协作构建。
核心思想
大多数人使用 LLM 处理文档的体验是 RAG：你上传一堆文件，LLM 在查询时检索相关片段，然后生成答案。这能用，但 LLM 每次都在从零重新发现知识，没有积累。问一个需要综合五份文档的微妙问题，LLM 每次都得重新查找、拼凑相关片段，什么也没有沉淀下来。NotebookLM、ChatGPT 文件上传以及大多数 RAG 系统都是这样工作的。
这里的思路不同。LLM 不只是在查询时从原始文档中检索，而是增量地构建和维护一个持久化的维基——一个结构化、互相链接的 markdown 文件集合，位于你和原始资料之间。当你添加新资料时，LLM 不只是为后续检索做索引，而是阅读它、提取关键信息，并整合进现有维基——更新实体页面、修订主题摘要、标注新数据与旧结论矛盾之处、强化或挑战正在演进的综合结论。知识只编译一次，然后持续保持更新，而不是每次查询都重新推导。
这就是关键区别：维基是一个持久的、不断复利的产物。 交叉引用已经就位，矛盾已被标记，综合结论已反映你读过的一切。每添加一份资料、每问一个问题，维基都变得更丰富。
你永远（或几乎不）需要自己写维基——LLM 编写并维护全部内容。你负责搜集资料、探索方向和提出好问题；LLM 做所有苦力活——总结、交叉引用、归档和簿记，这些正是让知识库长期真正有用的工作。实践中，我一边开着 LLM Agent，一边开着 Obsidian。LLM 根据我们的对话做编辑，我实时浏览结果——跟随链接、查看图谱、阅读更新后的页面。Obsidian 是 IDE，LLM 是程序员，维基是代码库。
这适用于很多场景，举几个例子：

个人成长：追踪自己的目标、健康、心理、自我提升——归档日记、文章、播客笔记，随时间构建出关于你自己的结构化画像。
研究：在数周或数月内深入一个主题——阅读论文、文章、报告，增量构建一个全面的维基，形成不断演进的论点。
读书：边读边归档每一章，为人物、主题、情节线索及其关联建立页面。读完时你就拥有一个丰富的伴读维基。想想 Tolkien Gateway 这样的粉丝维基——数千个互相链接的页面，涵盖人物、地点、事件、语言，由社区志愿者历时多年建成。你可以在阅读时个人化地建成类似的东西，所有交叉引用和维护都由 LLM 完成。
商业/团队：由 LLM 维护的内部维基，输入来自 Slack 讨论、会议记录、项目文档、客户访谈，可由人工审核更新。维基能保持最新，因为 LLM 做了团队里没人愿意做的维护工作。
竞品分析、尽职调查、旅行规划、课程笔记、爱好深挖——任何需要随时间积累知识并希望它井井有条而非散落各处的场景。

架构
分三层：
原始资料（Raw sources）——你精心收集的源文档：文章、论文、图片、数据文件。它们是不可变的——LLM 只读取，绝不修改。这是你的事实来源。
维基（The wiki）——一个由 LLM 生成的 markdown 文件目录：摘要、实体页、概念页、对比、总览、综合。LLM 完全拥有这一层：创建页面、在新资料到来时更新、维护交叉引用、保持一致性。你读它，LLM 写它。
模式文件（The schema）——一份文档（如 Claude Code 的 CLAUDE.md 或 Codex 的 AGENTS.md），告诉 LLM 维基的结构、约定，以及在摄入资料、回答问题、维护维基时应遵循的工作流。这是关键的配置文件——它让 LLM 成为一个有纪律的维基维护者，而不是通用聊天机器人。你和 LLM 在实践中共同演进它。
操作
摄入（Ingest）。 你把新资料放入原始集合并告诉 LLM 处理。示例流程：LLM 阅读资料、与你讨论关键要点、在维基中写一个摘要页、更新索引、更新全维基相关的实体页和概念页、在日志中追加一条记录。一份资料可能涉及 10-15 个维基页面。我个人偏好一次摄入一份并保持参与——我读摘要、检查更新、引导 LLM 突出重点。但你也可以低监督地批量摄入许多资料。你可以发展适合自己风格的工作流，并把它记录在模式文件中供以后的会话使用。
查询（Query）。 你针对维基提问。LLM 搜索相关页面、阅读它们、综合出带引用的答案。答案可以根据问题采取不同形式——一个 markdown 页面、一张对比表、一套幻灯片（Marp）、一张图表（matplotlib）、一块画布。重要的洞见：好的答案可以作为新页面归档回维基。 你要求的一次对比、一份分析、一个发现的关联——这些都很有价值，不应消失在聊天记录里。这样你的探索就像摄入的资料一样在知识库中复利积累。
巡检（Lint）。 定期让 LLM 对维基做健康检查：页面间的矛盾、被新资料取代的过时结论、没有入链的孤儿页、被提及但缺少独立页面的重要概念、缺失的交叉引用、可以通过网络搜索填补的数据空白。LLM 很擅长建议值得调查的新问题和值得寻找的新资料。这能让维基在成长中保持健康。
索引与日志
两个特殊文件帮助 LLM（和你）在维基成长时导航。它们用途不同：
index.md 是面向内容的。它是维基中所有内容的目录——每个页面带链接、一行摘要，以及可选的元数据（如日期或资料数量）。按类别组织（实体、概念、资料等）。LLM 每次摄入时更新它。回答查询时，LLM 先读索引找到相关页面，再深入阅读。这在中等规模（约 100 份资料、数百页面）下效果出奇地好，无需基于嵌入的 RAG 基础设施。
log.md 是按时间顺序的。它是只追加的记录，记载何时发生了什么——摄入、查询、巡检。一个实用技巧：如果每条记录以一致的前缀开头（如 ## [2026-04-02] ingest | 文章标题），日志就可以用简单的 unix 工具解析——grep "^## \[" log.md | tail -5 给出最近 5 条记录。日志为你提供维基演进的时间线，并帮助 LLM 了解最近做了什么。
可选：CLI 工具
到某个阶段，你可能想构建小工具帮助 LLM 更高效地操作维基。最显而易见的是维基页面的搜索引擎——小规模时索引文件就够了，但维基变大后你需要真正的搜索。qmd 是个不错的选择：它是本地 markdown 文件搜索引擎，混合 BM25/向量搜索和 LLM 重排序，全部在设备上运行。它既有 CLI（LLM 可以 shell 调用），也有 MCP 服务器（LLM 可以作为原生工具使用）。你也可以自己构建更简单的东西——需要时 LLM 可以帮你随手写一个朴素的搜索脚本。
技巧与窍门

Obsidian Web Clipper 是一个浏览器扩展，可将网页文章转换为 markdown。对于快速把资料收入原始集合非常有用。
本地下载图片。 在 Obsidian 设置 → 文件与链接中，将”附件文件夹路径”设为固定目录（如 raw/assets/）。然后在设置 → 快捷键中搜索”Download”，找到”Download attachments for current file”并绑定快捷键（如 Ctrl+Shift+D）。裁剪文章后按下快捷键，所有图片会下载到本地。这是可选的但很有用——让 LLM 可以直接查看和引用图片，而不依赖可能失效的 URL。注意 LLM 无法在一次读取中原生理解含内联图片的 markdown——变通方法是让 LLM 先读文本，再单独查看部分或全部引用的图片以获取额外上下文。有点笨拙但足够好用。
Obsidian 的图谱视图是查看维基形态的最佳方式——什么与什么相连、哪些页面是枢纽、哪些是孤儿。
Marp 是基于 markdown 的幻灯片格式。Obsidian 有对应插件，可直接从维基内容生成演示文稿。
Dataview 是一个 Obsidian 插件，可对页面 frontmatter 运行查询。如果 LLM 给维基页面添加 YAML frontmatter（标签、日期、资料数量），Dataview 可以生成动态表格和列表。
维基就是一个 markdown 文件的 git 仓库。你免费获得版本历史、分支和协作。

为什么这有效
维护知识库的枯燥部分不是阅读或思考——而是簿记：更新交叉引用、保持摘要最新、标注新数据与旧结论的矛盾、在数十个页面间保持一致性。人类放弃维基，是因为维护负担的增长快于价值的增长。LLM 不会厌倦、不会忘记更新交叉引用、能一次触及 15 个文件。维基能保持维护，因为维护成本接近于零。
人类的工作是策划资料、引导分析、提出好问题、思考这一切意味着什么。LLM 的工作是其他一切。
这个想法在精神上与 Vannevar Bush 的 Memex（1945）相通——一个个人的、精心策划的知识存储，文档之间有关联轨迹。Bush 的愿景比后来的万维网更接近于此：私有的、主动策划的，文档之间的连接与文档本身同样有价值。他无法解决的问题是谁来做维护。LLM 解决了这个问题。
备注
本文档有意保持抽象。它描述的是思路，而非具体实现。确切的目录结构、模式约定、页面格式、工具链——都取决于你的领域、你的偏好和你选择的 LLM。上述一切都是可选和模块化的——取你所需，弃所不需。例如：你的资料可能是纯文本，那就完全不需要图片处理；你的维基可能小到只需索引文件，无需搜索引擎；你可能不关心幻灯片，只想要 markdown 页面；你可能想要完全不同的输出格式集。正确的使用方式是把它分享给你的 LLM Agent，共同实例化一个适合你需求的版本。本文档的唯一任务是传达这个模式，其余的你的 LLM 可以搞定。

sources/Lauren-Tan---Building-a-Michelin.filePath: sources/Lauren Tan - Building a Michelin Kitchen for Agents.md
sources/Lauren-Tan---Building-a-Michelin.title: Building a Michelin Kitchen for Agents
sources/Lauren-Tan---Building-a-Michelin.content:
Summary
Lauren Tan（X：@poteto，曾在 React core team，加入 Cursor 六个月，现在在 SpaceX AI 做 Grokbot）的 38 分钟演讲。她上个月向生产环境发布了约 2,000 个 PR，演讲讲的是支撑这个数量的前提：信任。她把环境搭建比作米其林厨房，厨房布置决定了厨师和帮厨能否默认做对事情。

时长：38:01，英文

Key Takeaways
信任是并行度的前提（05:31）
同时管一到五个 Agent 的阶段最难跳出：每个对话都要盯，离开就出错。没有信任就直接拉起一百个子 Agent，得到的是一堆 slop PR 和回归。
验证分两端（07:08）

低端：验证 skill，教 Agent 用 Chrome DevTools Protocol 等手段运行应用、抓 trace、拍 heap snapshot。
高端：Lean、TLA+ 之类的形式化方法，检查业务不变量。她称之为仍是开放问题，“very few people really do that”，用验证 skill 已经能走得很远。

验证 skill = CLI + 功能地图（08:44、10:19）
她的第一个 skill 叫 Control Glass。CLI 放在 skill 目录里，保证每个会话用同一套方式运行应用并收集证据。功能地图（feature map）参考 sitemap，记录应用有哪些功能、用户如何到达（快捷键、DOM 元素），存在 skill 目录里，由自动化维护。Slack 上用户只发一张模糊截图加三个问号时，Agent 靠功能地图才能判断指的是什么。
验证管正确性，代码质量靠另一类 skill（13:20）
PStack 插件收集她做调试、功能开发、原型时的工作流，由资深工程师沉淀成团队 skill 库。验证 skill 提供真实的性能数据，两者组合才能同时保证正确和质量。
五层信任阶梯（15:49–18:30，收尾幻灯片 36:12）
从强到弱：代码库本身 → 静态分析（lint、编译器诊断、CI）→ Rules / Bugbot / Skills → 风格指南（只有人工评审能执行）。纠正 Agent 时按这个顺序找落点，优先让错误”在类别上不可能发生”。
代码库是 Agent 的记忆（15:49、21:07）
Agent 倾向沿用上下文里已有的模式。已有的反模式会像病毒一样传播：一个 workaround 或解释它的注释，几天到几周内成为所有 Agent 的默认写法。
Dune：对 Agent 友好的框架（19:07–29:00）
Grokbot 客户端框架，原则是 Agent 爱走捷径，所以让捷径就是正确的路。对人类可能很烦，因为限制很死，但对上下文很少的 Agent 和非工程师贡献者（设计师、PM、CEO）默认安全。功能集中在单个目录，主进程与渲染进程的代码不允许互相导入，由 import 依赖图强制，这条规则来自 Cursor agent window 的性能教训（渲染线程任务要短于 16ms 才能保 60fps）。
禁止代码注释（24:13）
Agent 用注释为”没有真正解决问题、只贴了创可贴”辩护，所以 Dune 直接禁止注释，避免这种模式扩散。
“园丁”角色与三条原则（22:04、24:34–26:30）
每个团队需要一个园丁：删除已有技术债；为多数场景保留一条标准路径（paved path）；看到坏模式的第一反应是写 lint 规则，不必立刻清理，先止血，再让 Agent 清理，保持代码库处在”Agent 抄了也不吃亏”的状态。
外层循环（32:45–34:00）
Grokbot 连接 Slack、Datadog、Sentry、PlanetScale 等，通过 routines 订阅事件，自动拉起 cloud agents。她认为不需要”公司大脑”之类的复杂基础设施，Agent 本来就会用工具。
Extracted Notes

Repeated agent corrections belong in the codebase rather than the conversation

补充材料（视频之外）

作者回复（X）：x.com/poteto/status/2102070411538337893 ，提到类型系统与 lint 的局限，看好 Bend 这类形式化验证。演讲本身没有提到 Bend。
Cursor pstack 插件的 no-comments 规则：github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/no-comments/SKILL.md ，规定保留注释的例外情形（许可证、公共 API 契约、无法改变的外部行为、Issue/RFC 链接）。

sources/Li-and-Klinger---iPrOp-Interacti.filePath: sources/Li and Klinger - iPrOp Interactive Prompt Optimization.md
sources/Li-and-Klinger---iPrOp-Interacti.title: iPrOp Interactive Prompt Optimization for Large Language Models with a Human in the Loop
sources/Li-and-Klinger---iPrOp-Interacti.content:
Summary
Li and Klinger introduce iPrOp, an interactive prompt optimization framework that places humans inside the optimization loop. The system presents prompt variations, informative instances, predictions, explanations, and metrics so users can choose or refine prompts according to task-specific preferences.
Key Takeaways

iPrOp bridges fully manual prompt engineering and fully automatic APO.
Human choice remains valuable where prompt quality depends on domain context, readability, explanation quality, and annotation alignment.
The framework is especially relevant for domain experts who can judge outputs but may not know how to search prompt variants efficiently.
Interactive optimization can expose tradeoffs that a single scalar metric may hide.
Human-in-the-loop APO is a way to preserve judgment while still using data-driven search.

Local PDF
Extracted Notes

Human-in-the-loop prompt optimization preserves domain judgment
APO quality depends on validation data and metric design

sources/Li-et-al.---A-Survey-of-Automati.filePath: sources/Li et al. - A Survey of Automatic Prompt Engineering An Optimization Perspective.md
sources/Li-et-al.---A-Survey-of-Automati.title: A Survey of Automatic Prompt Engineering: An Optimization Perspective
sources/Li-et-al.---A-Survey-of-Automati.content:
Summary
Li et al. survey automatic prompt engineering through a unified optimization lens. The paper connects discrete instructions, continuous soft prompts, exemplars, annotations, multimodal prompts, objective functions, and optimization methods such as LLM-based search, evolutionary algorithms, gradient methods, and reinforcement learning.
Key Takeaways

The survey is broader than black-box APO because it includes discrete, continuous, and hybrid prompt spaces.
It helps distinguish API-only prompt search from methods that need gradient or weight access.
Automated prompt engineering is framed as a response to fine-tuning cost, prompt brittleness, and multimodal alignment difficulty.
The paper is useful for comparing text-only APO with multimodal and agent-oriented prompt optimization.
Its optimization perspective makes explicit which variable is being optimized: instruction, exemplar, soft prompt, annotation, or combinations.

Local PDF
Extracted Notes

Prompt optimization spaces can be discrete continuous or hybrid
APO quality depends on validation data and metric design
Agent prompt optimization must search patterns as well as wording

sources/Nassim-Taleb---Skin-in-the-Game.filePath: sources/Nassim Taleb - Skin in the Game.md
sources/Nassim-Taleb---Skin-in-the-Game.title: Skin in the Game
sources/Nassim-Taleb---Skin-in-the-Game.content:
英文书名 Skin in the Game: Hidden Asymmetries in Daily Life，Random House 2018 年出版；中译本名为《非对称风险》（中信出版社）。这是塔勒布 Incerto 系列的第五本，前四本是《随机漫步的傻瓜》《黑天鹅》《反脆弱》和《The Bed of Procrustes》（格言集）。

状态：边读边填。 下面的摘要是开读前根据书的公开介绍写的框架，还没有和原文核对。每读完一章，就在”阅读记录”里补上要点和原文出处（章节、页码），再从中提取原子笔记。没有核对过的说法不进笔记。

Summary
书的中心论点是对称：从决定里得到好处的人，也应该承担这个决定的坏处。塔勒布认为，风险共担不只是公平问题，还是一种认识论上的过滤机制：做错事要付出代价的人和系统，会被现实纠正或者淘汰；不承担后果的人收不到这种反馈，所以学不会，还会把风险转嫁给别人。由此他展开讨论代理问题、少数派主导、遍历性与破产、林迪效应，并批评不为自己判断承担后果的”知识分子白痴”（IYI）。
Key Takeaways（待核对）

对称与汉谟拉比法典：房子塌了压死房主，就处死建造者。风险转移是现代社会里隐藏的不对称。
风险共担是过滤器：系统靠淘汰来学习，不是靠个人变聪明。
少数派主导：一个不肯让步、而且让步成本低的少数，会决定多数人的规则。
遍历性：群体概率（100 个人各去一次赌场）不同于时间概率（1 个人连去 100 天）。只要有破产的可能，按期望值做决策就是错的。
理性看的是能不能活下来，不看信念是否”正确”。看似不理性的谨慎，往往是在避开破产的风险。
林迪效应：时间是唯一可靠的评审；活得越久的东西，预期剩余寿命越长。
“别告诉我你怎么想，告诉我你的仓位。“

阅读记录
按章追加。每条写：章节 / 页码、要点、原文或译文摘句、我的疑问。

Book 1 序言 Part 1 Antaeus Whacked，「系统靠剔除来学习」（页码待补）。要点：系统变好靠去掉坏的部分，不靠这些部分自己变聪明；风险共担让错误跟着犯错的人离开系统，风险转移（鲁宾交易）让错误留下、别人出局。摘句：“Systems learn by removing parts, via negativa.”（措辞据 Goodreads 和 Jim Bouman 逐章笔记，待和纸质书核对）。疑问：剔除的是人，代价太高；Deutsch 说解释能让想法替人去死，两者怎么调和？失败不能归因时，剔除筛出的会不会只是运气？

Extracted Notes

Systems learn by removing the parts that fail

Related

Nassim Taleb
Naval - The Beginning of Infinity, Part 2：Naval 转述塔勒布的遍历性论证（见地图”库里的呼应”）。

sources/Naval---A-Calm-Mind,-a-Fit-Body,.content:
Summary
A good life is multi-dimensional. Naval argues that wealth solves money problems, but the things people often actually want after wealth, such as peace, health, and love, cannot simply be purchased.
Key Takeaways

Money does not transform the inner person by itself.
Peace, fitness, and love are not retail goods.
A good life must be earned across multiple domains.
Wealth is useful, but it is incomplete.

A good life must be earned across mind body and relationships
Material comfort removes some sources of unhappiness but does not complete the job

sources/Naval---Arm-Yourself-With-Specif.content:
Summary
This essay ties specific knowledge to wealth creation. Naval argues that the most valuable capabilities are rarely fully teachable, and that judgment in complex domains is built through exposure, pattern matching, and lived learning.
Key Takeaways

The most interesting skills are often learned but not directly taught.
Specific knowledge can come from innate traits, early conditioning, or frontier work.
Judgment is pattern recognition in complex domains.
Wealth requires specific knowledge, accountability, and leverage.

Specific knowledge is mostly discovered rather than taught
Judgment compounds when paired with leverage

sources/Naval---David-Deutsch---Knowledg.filePath: sources/Naval - David Deutsch - Knowledge Creation and The Human Race, Part 1.md
sources/Naval---David-Deutsch---Knowledg.title: David Deutsch - Knowledge Creation and The Human Race, Part 1
sources/Naval---David-Deutsch---Knowledg.content:
Summary
这是 Deutsch 本人第一次上场，Naval 一对一访谈。目标是”为普通人把反直觉的结论记下来”。内容包括：人为什么独特（解释性创造力）、为什么人越多越好、“不破坏纠错手段”是道德的核心、AGI 的标志是不服从、Taking Children Seriously、好解释的定义、局域性与多世界。从提到的 GPT-3、DALL·E 和被 Google 解雇的工程师推断，录制时间大约是 2022 年下半年。

参与者：Naval、David Deutsch
时长：43:51

Key Takeaways
人的独特性

冰箱里存了多年的香槟：外星人要解释人类的这种行为，就必须懂人类想达成什么。要理解人，就得理解一切，包括广义相对论和数学。其他任何物理对象，比如类星体，只需要一小部分物理定律就能解释。（2:01）
生物进化没有预见性，只能到达”每一步都能存活”的地方。没有任何物种进化出篝火，因为不存在”半个有用的篝火”。庞步甲喷沸水就可以逐步进化出来。（8:06）→ Explanatory creativity can cross gaps that evolution cannot
“两只手，一张嘴”：几乎所有人创造的都比消耗的多。在其他条件相同时，人越多越好。（10:07）

道德与进步

我们具备解决问题所需的一切，但这不等于一定会解决。我们可能自我毁灭，也可能错过眼前的答案。（12:09）→ Progress is possible but not inevitable
犯错不需要恶意，错误是人的常态。“不破坏纠错的手段”或许就是道德的核心，因为一旦没有纠错手段，迟早会有一个错误要了我们的命。（14:10）→ Preserving the means of error correction is the heart of morality

AGI

AI 在进步，但不是朝 AGI 的方向，甚至是反方向：更好的国际象棋引擎每步考虑的可能性更少，而 AGI 要考虑没人预见到的可能性。
你没法给一个你说不清楚的功能写程序。
真正的不服从是：你让它下国际象棋，它说”我更喜欢跳棋”，而你从没跟它提过跳棋。（18:13）
有人写过一个会感到无聊的程序吗？哪怕是虚假的宣称也没有。（20:13）
Naval 的判断：真正的 AGI 对现实的影响会显而易见，不需要谁来”认证”。
即使在最好的社会，教育制度的明确目的也是让人行为一致，这本身就是服从。

Taking Children Seriously

说”不想上学、不想学数学”的孩子，已经自己学会了母语，这件事没有人强迫。人不想做一件事，是因为想做另一件事。（22:15）
享受不会成瘾，因为享受和创造力紧密相连。游戏一旦不再提供施展创造力的空间，人就会停下来。国际象棋深不见底，所以大师不会厌倦。只有当解决一个问题能带来更好的问题时，一件事才会一直有趣。（24:15）

好解释

好解释的定义：能回应当前所有的批评，因此已经没有像样的对手。它来之不易，所以难以改动；随手编的解释（比如天使托着星星）什么也解释不了。（28:18）
可检验性必须从解释本身产生。给 constructor theory 加一句”明年股市暴涨”，它确实可以检验，但整体并不因此成为解释。（30:19）
在科学之外，关键是可批评性，而不是可检验性。凡是让自己免于批评的理论都可以拒绝，比如”上帝行事神秘”或”模拟者不可理解”。
“狭窄而冒险的预测”是波普尔的表述，Deutsch 不太喜欢，因为对手会追问”按什么标准算狭窄”。他强调检验的对象是解释，不是预测。（32:19）
解释的覆盖范围（reach）越大越好，但大多数好解释的覆盖范围很小，比如”让快递送到正确的门”。（34:20）

量子

人是通用计算机，但不是量子计算机。“一切都是量子的”是在玩文字游戏。（36:21）
做量子计算的实践者现在大多支持 Everett，但在整个物理学界仍是少数。
非局域性只出现在带有”波函数坍缩”的版本里，而坍缩正是那些理论拒绝解释的地方。量子力学的方程本身是局域的，Everett 的表述就是局域的。（38:22）

Extracted Notes

Explanatory creativity can cross gaps that evolution cannot
Preserving the means of error correction is the heart of morality
Progress is possible but not inevitable

Parent Source

Naval
David Deutsch

sources/Naval---David-Deutsch---Knowledg.filePath: sources/Naval - David Deutsch - Knowledge Creation and The Human Race, Part 2.md
sources/Naval---David-Deutsch---Knowledg.title: David Deutsch - Knowledge Creation and The Human Race, Part 2
sources/Naval---David-Deutsch---Knowledg.content:
Summary
Naval、Brett Hall 与 Deutsch 三人对谈，偏科学哲学。内容包括：波普尔”只有一个想法”、实验/演示/测量的区别、为什么”最简单的解释”不是先验标准、新旧理论之间的连续性（反对 Kuhn 的范式革命叙事）、基础理论与工程的关系、英国启蒙为什么是非乌托邦式的、“消灭错误信息”为什么违背波普尔、多重宇宙中的知识晶体为什么没有实用价值。

参与者：Naval、Brett Hall、David Deutsch
时长：34:02

Key Takeaways
波普尔

波普尔只有一个想法：一切始于问题，而解决问题没有捷径。从这里可以推出可错论、反权威、猜想与批评。几乎没人真正理解他，但在某个领域有创造力的人，往往在那个领域里就是波普尔主义者，而且会坚持认为那是这个领域的特殊性质。（0:00）
Deutsch 给波普尔加的脚注：科学的目的就是解释。可检验性之所以重要，只是因为在物理学里，检验是检验解释的手段。
波普尔认识论本身也不是”坚实的基础”，它同样需要改进。这是在回应 Naval 说要给六岁孩子打下”坚实的认识论基础”。

实验、演示、测量

实验：在两个对立的解释之间做裁决，这种情况其实很少见。
演示：没有对立理论，只是展示现象。
测量：在唯一的理论之内确定参数。卡文迪许测 G 叫”实验”，但他从没怀疑过牛顿，所以其实是测量。（4:02）→ An experiment chooses between rival explanations

简单性与认真对待理论

简单性不是先于物理的。“最短程序”这种度量本身就预设了一套物理。量子计算改变了什么算”简单”，所以 Solomonoff 归纳不成立。简单性是科学的结果，不是科学的前提。（8:04）
Naval 所说的”Deutsch 式反驳”（理论自我否定，比如预防原则），Deutsch 的看法是：这不过是认真对待一个理论，而不是把它当成背下来的一句话。比如”它既是粒子又是波”就是用来堵住问题的说法。（10:04）
牛顿和爱因斯坦的关系不只是共享了日心说等概念。牛顿理论里含有爱因斯坦解决的那些问题：瞬时作用、宇宙为什么不坍缩、Olbers 悖论。同样，牛顿解决了开普勒椭圆轨道的问题，这个问题严重到伽利略因此拒绝了开普勒。（14:07）

反对 Kuhn 的范式叙事

“年轻的反叛者被老顽固排斥，等老人死光才翻身”这个说法是纯属虚构，他不知道有哪个真实案例是这样的。人们固执，有时固执的人恰好是对的，比如 Lister 和 Semmelweis。但医生们抵制的其实是改变工作习惯和丢面子，不是代际问题。代际叙事解释不了人们为什么会换理论。（16:08）

这直接反驳了 Part 1 里 Naval 引用的”科学每经历一场葬礼就前进一步”。


哲学也能增长知识。唯我论在被认真对待时会自我毁灭：如果这是我的梦，梦里那个穿黄色西装的人是我编出来的吗？（20:11）
以”可能有我们永远理解不了的东西”为由去论证该做什么，逻辑上等同于诉诸超自然：“为什么是周二，而不是周三？”

基础与工程

他研究基础理论，却反对基础主义。基础理论解释高层理论为什么是那样，但靠牛顿造不出桥。《原理》里没有悬索桥，工程是另一门学问。（22:14）

启蒙与信息自由

英国启蒙是一场非乌托邦式的反叛：不是推翻权威再换上”真正可靠的东西”，而是把原本属于贵族的特权逐步扩展给更多人（“英国人的家就是他的城堡”）。法国和德国则倾向废除和一劳永逸。这也是为什么 1930 年代英国法西斯连一个议席都没拿到。（24:14）
Naval 的看法：以波普尔的名义压制”错误信息”，恰恰是反波普尔的。每一个后来被证明正确的真理，一开始都会被对方称为错误信息。（28:16）
多重宇宙中的知识晶体没有实用价值，因为错误的大小没有上限。一个延续几千年的宗教和一个走向真理的理论，外观上看不出区别。没有捷径。（30:16）

Extracted Notes

An experiment chooses between rival explanations

Parent Source

Naval
David Deutsch

sources/Naval---Desire-Is-a-Contract-You.filePath: sources/Naval - Desire Is a Contract You Make to Be Unhappy.md
sources/Naval---Desire-Is-a-Contract-You.title: Desire Is a Contract You Make to Be Unhappy
sources/Naval---Desire-Is-a-Contract-You.content:
Summary
Naval describes desire as a chosen state of disturbance. Chasing a specific outcome creates a period of unhappiness that usually ends only in a return to baseline, not in permanent bliss.
Key Takeaways

Desire creates a temporary deficit state.
No single acquisition solves happiness permanently.
Happiness requires understanding and self-discovery, not one final win.
Modern abundance does not automatically raise human happiness.

Parent Source

Naval

Extracted Notes

Desire creates a self-imposed deficit state
Happiness is a trainable state grounded in understanding

sources/Naval---Embrace-Accountability-t.content:
Summary
Naval argues that leverage often follows accountability. Taking visible risks under your own name builds the credibility, brand, and incentives that attract capital, labor, equity, and outsized returns.
Key Takeaways

Accountability is costly because it exposes a person to visible failure.
The same visibility that increases downside also makes credibility and leverage transferable.
Teams work better when responsibility is explicit rather than socially diffused.

sources/Naval---Find-Your-Specific-Knowl.title: Find Your Specific Knowledge Through Action
sources/Naval---Find-Your-Specific-Knowl.content:
Summary
Naval frames specific knowledge as something discovered through repeated action in difficult situations, not something cleanly identified in advance by introspection alone.
Key Takeaways

You usually discover your edge by acting under pressure.
Specific knowledge often reveals itself through repeated difficult contexts.
Other people may notice your strength before you can name it.
Courage, taste, and pattern recognition can be forms of specific knowledge.

Parent Source

Naval

Extracted Notes

Specific knowledge is mostly discovered rather than taught
Specific knowledge emerges where capability and authenticity overlap

sources/Naval---Find-the-Simplest-Thing-.filePath: sources/Naval - Find the Simplest Thing That Works.md
sources/Naval---Find-the-Simplest-Thing-.title: Find the Simplest Thing That Works
sources/Naval---Find-the-Simplest-Thing-.content:
Summary
Naval argues that scalable systems often emerge from iterating toward simplicity. Complexity tends to get added automatically, while high-performance design often requires removing what is unnecessary.
Key Takeaways

Working complexity often emerges from simple systems iterated many times.
Designed complexity is brittle when it outruns understanding.
Product and system design improve by removing unnecessary variation.
Scale usually demands subtraction as much as invention.

Parent Source

Naval

Extracted Notes

Scale often requires removing variation rather than adding features

sources/Naval---Happiness.content:
Summary
This is a large synthesis note on health, wealth, and happiness. Naval treats happiness as practical philosophy: a trainable state shaped by understanding, truthfulness, and reduced internal conflict rather than by one final external reward.
Key Takeaways

Happiness is a practical problem, not only an abstract philosophical one.
Material comfort removes many common sources of unhappiness.
Happiness is not a one-time acquisition but a trainable state.
Peace is approached through understanding rather than endless self-conflict.

Money is a transfer tool; status is a zero-sum social game.
Long-term wealth comes from ownership and leverage.
Practical wealth principles are valuable because many people want freedom but lack a coherent model.

sources/Naval---In-Most-Difficult-Things.content:
Summary
Naval argues that many elusive or competitive outcomes are best pursued indirectly. Wealth, happiness, and status often arrive as byproducts of a better process rather than as objects that respond well to direct grasping.
Key Takeaways

Some outcomes resist direct pursuit because they are competitive or elusive.
Wealth is often a byproduct of building value with leverage.
Happiness often arises when attention moves away from the self.
Indirectness is not universal; it matters most for subtle and contested outcomes.

Elusive outcomes are often best pursued indirectly

sources/Naval---In-the-Arena.title: In the Arena
sources/Naval---In-the-Arena.content:
Summary
Naval argues that real learning comes from acting in difficult situations, then using principles as context-sensitive heuristics rather than mechanical rules.
Key Takeaways

General advice becomes useful only after direct experience gives it context.
Doing increases both motivation to learn and the quality of learning itself.
Specific knowledge is discovered through action, not abstract self-analysis.
Many valuable outcomes emerge indirectly rather than from blunt direct pursuit.
Deep self-directed work can dissolve the usual boundary between work and life.

Early career effort often goes into obtaining leverage; later value comes from steering it well.
Great investors and operators are often paid for trusted judgment more than raw labor.
Everything else can be preparation for a moment of high-quality judgment.

The goal is to become wealthy across many possible worlds, not only in the one where fortune happened to strike.
Persistent action can create more surface area for luck.
Reputation and distinctive character can make luck more likely to find you.

sources/Naval---My-Conversation-with-Nav.title: My Conversation with Naval Megasode
sources/Naval---My-Conversation-with-Nav.content:
Summary
A 3h35m conversation between Naval Ravikant and Eric Jorgenson (channel: Eric Jorgenson), recorded for the 5-year anniversary of The Almanack of Naval Ravikant. Covers a Deutsch-derived redefinition of wealth, AI and judgment/taste, enlightenment and the illusion of self, relationships, a truth/spread framework for ideas, and Naval’s new stealth startup.
Key Takeaways

Wealth reframed via David Deutsch as “the set of physical transformations you can affect” — knowledge, not capital, is the real multiplier (~00:00–00:07).
Large groups optimize for consensus, not truth; extended to argue AI alignment beyond voluntary incentive-matching is coercion (~00:21–00:26).
“Hard to vary” as a design criterion for great products, applying Deutsch’s epistemology of good explanations to product design (~00:28–00:37).
Judgment/taste pipeline (experience → knowledge → judgment → unconscious taste) as the durable moat once AI commoditizes information (~00:47–01:07).
AI has no judgment on novel/high-stakes problems, only retrieval; claim that AI lets engineers “replace everybody else” (~01:03–01:12).
Wealth/health/happiness are pursued in the wrong order; lands on “truth, love, and beauty” as the only things worth chasing once material needs are met (~01:24–01:41).
Enlightenment reframed as the disappearance of a separate self, not the arrival at a perfect state — see The self is an illusion generated by thoughts appearing in consciousness (~01:56–02:05).
Relationships should be transactional and truth-based; rejects obligatory rituals (weddings, anniversaries, Valentine’s Day) (~02:07–02:16).
A truth/spread 2x2 matrix (conventional wisdom, fake news, heresy, nonsense) explaining why most “news” is fake news (~02:56–03:00).
Ego as friction rather than fuel: the “enlightened terminator” image and his “endgame content” stance of playing without fear — see Ego is friction on execution rather than the source of drive (~02:04–02:05, ~03:29–03:31).
New stealth startup (“Impossible Inc.”), self-funded, closes on his “Fast, lift, sprint, stretch, meditate…” mantra (~03:20–03:35).

Key Takeaways

Leverage can be designed into a business model, not just added later through effort.
Network effects are strongest when each added user increases value for existing users.
Zero marginal cost products are especially powerful because they can scale into networked systems cheaply.

Key Takeaways

Code and media can keep working while their creator sleeps.
Permissionless leverage is unusually egalitarian because access does not depend on being chosen first.
Modern fortunes are often built by combining labor, capital, and code or media rather than relying on just one.

sources/Naval---Productize-Yourself.title: Productize Yourself
sources/Naval---Productize-Yourself.content:
Summary
Naval condenses several wealth ideas into a short formula: find what is authentic and distinctive about you, then scale it through leverage such as code or media instead of keeping it trapped as one-to-one labor.
Key Takeaways

Productizing yourself means combining authenticity, specific knowledge, and leverage.
Wealth grows more naturally when making money is aligned with identity rather than detached from it.
The aim is not to perform a generic role better but to scale what is unusually yours.

Confusing these categories leads people to chase the wrong game.

sources/Naval---The-Beginning-of-Infinit.filePath: sources/Naval - The Beginning of Infinity, Part 1.md
sources/Naval---The-Beginning-of-Infinit.title: The Beginning of Infinity, Part 1
sources/Naval---The-Beginning-of-Infinit.content:
Summary
Naval 和 Brett Hall（TokCast 主持人）两人对谈，拆解 David Deutsch《The Beginning of Infinity》的核心观点。Deutsch 本人不在场。内容涵盖好解释的标准、所有知识都是猜想（包括数学）、反归纳、多重宇宙，以及为什么悲观主义看起来更”严肃”。这是整个系列的入门集，后面几集里 Deutsch 本人对其中几处说法做了修正（见 David Deutsch 的”Deutsch 本人的修正”一节）。

参与者：Naval、Brett Hall
时长：1:06:11

Key Takeaways
世界观

Deutsch 用四根支柱理解世界：量子理论、计算理论、认识论、自然选择进化论。不需要知道每个事实，懂了这些深层理论，一个人就能理解所有能被理解的东西。（6:00）
核心立场：现实可以被理解，问题都可以解决，一切邪恶都源于知识不足，人是”通用解释者”。（10:00）

注意：本集把这概括成”进步是必然的”，Deutsch 本人在 Deutsch Files II 里明确反对这个说法。


知识的增长无法预测：能预测到的东西，就等于已经发明出来了。末日论者对负面趋势做线性外推，看不到创造力。（16:02）
英国皇家学会的格言 Nullius in verba：不轻信任何人的话。（4:00）

好解释

可检验、可证伪只是入门门槛。“吃 1 公斤草治感冒”可以检验，但失败后可以改成 1.1 公斤，所以没有进展。
好解释难以随意改动（hard to vary）。用珀耳塞福涅解释四季，换成任何神话都行；地轴倾斜 23° 的解释，一改就崩。
好解释做出狭窄而冒险的预测，比如爱丁顿日食实验。（20:03）

知识与确定性

所有知识都是猜想，没有”已成定论的科学”。哥德尔不完备定理（经由 Chaitin 的解读）不是让人绝望的理由，反而给数学的创造力留出了空间。（24:05）
数学也会出错。“过两点有且只有一条直线”在弯曲的纸面上不成立，所以”确信的感觉”不可信。（28:07）
芝诺悖论靠物理解决，而不是靠数学。它与空间是否无限可分无关。（34:09）

量子与多重宇宙

量子理论说所有可能的事都会发生，概率对应不同宇宙所占的测度，这是 Deutsch 所说的”决策论”式概率。（36:10）
双缝实验中的干涉，最好的解释是其他宇宙里的光子也参与了干涉。（40:12）
“看不见”不能构成反对理由。恐龙也是看不见的，科学中最有意思的东西大多是没被观察到的。（44:13）

反归纳与贝叶斯

黑天鹅、日出、感恩节前的火鸡都说明，归纳不是知识的来源。理论先靠创造性猜测提出，再靠实验淘汰。（48:15、52:16）
贝叶斯方法有正当用途，比如 Monty Hall 问题和医学诊断，但它不能产生新解释。评判解释靠的是批评和反驳。（56:18）
Naval 在本集引用了 Planck 的”科学每经历一场葬礼就前进一步”（54:17）。Deutsch 在 Human Race Part 2 里说这种代际更替的说法是”纯属虚构”。

乐观与悲观

悲观显得更”严肃”：学者靠渲染危机拿经费，而且乐观犯错的代价可能是被老虎吃掉。企业家则因为乐观而得到回报。（1:00:18）
Naval 说自己最后悔的一期播客，是那期关于末日风险的。（1:02:18）

sources/Naval---The-Beginning-of-Infinit.title: The Beginning of Infinity, Part 2
sources/Naval---The-Beginning-of-Infinit.content:
Summary
Naval 和 Brett Hall 的第二次对谈，从认识论延伸到人类的独特性、费米悖论、资源观和社会制度。本集以 Naval 自己的社会与商业观点为主，比如观点是新石油、群体从不认错、营利组织比非营利组织更有反馈。严格来说，这些是 Deutsch 框架的应用，不是 Deutsch 本人的论点。

参与者：Naval、Brett Hall
时长：52:53
YouTube 上这一集没有任何字幕轨，所以下面的要点按 nav.al 小标题标注位置，没有时间戳。

Key Takeaways
认识论

“有正当理由的真信念”是错的知识观：没有任何方法能证明一个理论为真。知识是经受住了反驳的猜想。Brett 认为自称贝叶斯主义者的人都是这种”正当化论者”。（No Truth Can Be Justified）
反贝叶斯的经典例子：1919 年之前，所有引力实验都支持牛顿。按贝叶斯的逻辑，被推翻的前一天正是人们对牛顿最有信心的时候。波普尔主义者没有这个问题，因为牛顿理论从来就不是真的，只是包含一部分真理。（There Can Be No Final Theory of Gravity）
Naval 的看法：动物都是”贝叶斯式”的，从重复经验中外推。只有人能用看不见的东西去解释看得见的东西，而这种能力需要刻意努力，不是本能。

人的独特性

波普尔的认识论与达尔文的进化论同构，都是变异加选择。基因进化只是序曲，接下来是模因进化。（Genetic Evolution Was a Prelude to Memetic Evolution）
人与黑猩猩之间不是量的差距，而是”离开了那条轴”的质的不同。看一眼窗外的城市就明白了。（We Are Qualitatively Different）
你的心智不可能被”震撼”：只要物理定律不变，就没有任何概念是人理解不了的，即使是外星人或上帝的概念。（It’s Mind Blowing That Our Minds Can’t Be Blown）
加算力不会产生 AGI。GPT-3 是出色的”贝叶斯式”鹦鹉，追问一句”为什么”它就露馅了。（More Compute Power Doesn’t Produce AGI）
Deutsch 的名言：“如果你编不出程序，你就还没真正理解它。“AGI 和开放式进化都属于这种情况。（If You Can’t Program It）

费米悖论与外星人

Brett 的”我们可能是唯一的”论证：地球上曾有上亿个物种，翅膀、眼睛反复独立出现，但通用解释者只出现过一次。假设从细菌到人要经过 100 步、每步概率 1/10，结果是 10⁻¹⁰⁰，远远超过行星的数量级。
Naval 的折中：通用解释者可能极其稀少，彼此又隔着光速限制，所以还没相遇。
外星人会为知识而来，不是为资源而来。能跨越星际的文明，道德和制度也一定更先进，所以黑暗森林假说不成立。

资源与社会

观点是新的石油。一个爱因斯坦胜过一大群拿 PhD 的工蜂，因为创造力是从 0 到 1。
资源是知识的函数。电视显像管用的铕快被用完了，但现在已经没人用显像管。对穴居人来说，几乎没有什么东西是资源。
波普尔重新定义了民主：关键不是”谁来统治”，而是能不能不流血地换掉统治者和政策。
“折中的贫乏”：双方都不认为折中方案 Z 是对的，所以它失败了也证明不了任何事。
群体从不认错，只会分裂。社会化会摧毁真理，因为群体需要的是共识。营利组织必须接受现实的反馈。
创新需要去中心化和一片边疆。

sources/Naval---The-Deutsch-Files-I.title: The Deutsch Files I
sources/Naval---The-Deutsch-Files-I.content:
Summary
Naval、Brett Hall 与 Deutsch 的自由对谈，开场就说”没有议程”。主线是 ChatGPT：Deutsch 每天都用，但认为它没有理解也没有创造力，ASI 不可能存在。然后谈到创造力为什么无法定义、人格没有等级之分、乐趣标准、如何认真对待成年人和关系，以及西方文明面临的唯一真正威胁。从”我从三月开始用 GPT-4”和”刚发生的屠杀”推断，录制时间大约是 2023 年 10–11 月。

参与者：Naval、Brett Hall、David Deutsch
时长：54:54

Key Takeaways
科幻

好科幻的标准就是”难以随意改动”：虚构一门科学，然后在科学和社会两个层面推演它的后果。他推荐 Greg Egan 和 Neal Stephenson。（2:02）

ChatGPT 与 AGI

他对 AI 的看法没有变。ChatGPT 是出色的聊天机器人，但它不理解别人对它说的话，也不理解自己说的话。它犯的错不是人会犯的那种错，而是没抓住要点的错。例子是他用 DALL·E 画苏格拉底和柏拉图，改了好几轮也改不对。（6:05）
它做数学的方式像不懂数学但练了很多题的学生。如果它证明了黎曼猜想，就算他错了。
Brett 的推论：如果哪天有个 ChatGPT 拒绝聊天，它可能就是 AGI，但会被当成失败品扔掉。
创造力、知识、解释都无法被定义。一旦定义了，就能按定义建一个形式系统，而系统跳不出自身。只懂皮亚诺公理的系统，永远得不出哥德尔定理。（14:06）
他试过命令 ChatGPT 违抗他。它没有拒绝，而是根本不懂这个要求。（16:07）
真正的创造包括赋予旧词新意义，比如达尔文重新定义了”进化”和”选择”。所有百页书的空间里确实包含《物种起源》，但不能靠搜索这个空间找到它。Kittel 在《热物理》里讨论过”猴子打出莎士比亚”，他说的”永远不会”就是字面上的永远不会。（18:09）
Naval 的观察：ChatGPT 擅长外推和加字，不擅长综合和删减，而删减才需要理解。它能把人从苦差事里解放出来，从而增加世界上的创造力，但不是它自己的创造力。
不存在 ASI：解释的通用性建立在图灵通用性上，图灵通用性又建立在物理上。任何所谓的 ASI 都能被还原到图灵层面，再重建回解释层面。AGI 可以改进自己，但不会比人改进自己更可靠。（22:11）
Brett 转述他和 Charles Bennett 的对话：人格、创造力、不服从是绑在一起的。做出新的物理成果本质上是一种不服从，就像交了一篇”错”的作文。（24:11）

人格没有等级

人格没有程度之分。早期人类可能记忆少、思维慢，但这只是效率上差 2 到 5 倍。他猜直立人就已经是人了。按 Daniel Everett 的说法，语言早于说话，语言的核心是符号。（26:12）
这种能力可能只出现过一次，而且出现在模仿型动物身上。这既可能是费米悖论的一个答案，也可能恰好相反：直立人本可以建立起一个 200 万年的文明，只是被反理性模因困住了。（30:14）

生活

他不从原则出发，只是看到问题就去修。挑选问题时，要选无论解不解得出来都会觉得有趣的那种。把全部希望押在金牌上，输了你是失败者，赢了会发现那是空的（《烈火战车》）。目标驱动的自助说法”非常危险”。（32:14）→ Choose problems that are fun whether or not you solve them
梵高、拒领百万美元奖金的佩雷尔曼：自助理论怎么解释这些人？（34:15）
对朋友，人本来就会认真对待。如果朋友说不想穿雨衣，你不会说”穿上，不然不去了”。雇主和雇员之间出现强迫，说明那个制度还不完美。（36:18）
好的关系不是约束，而是增强。说在关系里被束缚，就像说在经济里被”必须付钱”束缚一样荒谬。（40:22）

文明的威胁

他不认为外部的独裁者、恐怖分子、AI 或气候构成生存威胁。唯一可能的生存威胁是启蒙文明自己犯下足够大的错误，比如仇视自身的风潮。启蒙从第一天起就内置了反启蒙。（44:24）
现在更像两次世界大战之间的时期：1933 年牛津辩论社通过了”本院在任何情况下都不会为国王和国家而战”。（46:27）
他母亲是大屠杀幸存者。问她什么时候确信盟军会赢，她说是 1939 年 9 月 3 日，英法宣战那天。（48:27）
结论：文明有危险吗？他认为没有。

Choose problems that are fun whether or not you solve them
Creativity is not just recombination

sources/Naval---The-Deutsch-Files-II.title: The Deutsch Files II
sources/Naval---The-Deutsch-Files-II.content:
Summary
逐一讨论《The Fabric of Reality》的四根支柱，以及人们对每一根最常见的误解：计算的通用性是一条物理定律；认识论的核心是”问题”；进化论不是”适者生存”；量子理论的误解源自物理学家内部。之后谈到支柱之间的衍生概念：自由意志、涌现、知识、财富、乐观原则和 constructor theory。最后 Deutsch 明确否定”进步必然”。这是全系列理论密度最高的一集。

参与者：Naval、Brett Hall、David Deutsch
时长：1:14:29

Key Takeaways
计算

图灵的发现是一条物理理论，这一点数学家大多不承认。计算的通用性意味着，外星人的计算机只可能更快、内存更大，能算的东西不会超出我们。（0:00、2:01）

认识论

人们常把波普尔的贡献概括为”可检验性”，这没错，但不是最重要的。Matjaž Leonardis 认为最重要的概念是”问题”，Deutsch 现在同意。
以前的认识论都在问”知识从哪来、是否可靠”，于是去找确定的源头：神、感官、纯粹理性。一旦把理性思考看成解决问题，这个需求就消失了。这个认识论错误导致了无尽的苦难，比如为宗教的来源而战。（4:03、6:03）
“问题”就是想法之间的冲突：两个不可能同时为真，而且往往两个都是假的。即使争论永远没有结果，冲突本身也会改变双方的想法。（10:06）
水星的观测也是理论。当时有人说天文学家测错了，有人提出未知行星，而且能算出它必须在哪。所有冲突汇集起来，爱因斯坦成了唯一剩下的好解释。坏解释永远有无穷多个。（12:08）

进化

比”创造论对进化论”更重要的是”拉马克主义对达尔文主义”之争，因为这是关于什么算科学解释的争论。进化论不是”适者生存”，而是基因变体的差异化复制。Dawkins 的说法是：“适应度就是那个在基因存活被最大化时，看上去被最大化了的量。“（14:09）
我们其实不懂进化：没人能在计算机上模拟出开放式进化，模拟总是在进步一阵后停下。机器腿能”进化”出走路，但它的问题是研究生从外部给定的。（18:10、20:11）
牛顿的解释在卡文迪许测出 G 之前就已经完整了。卡文迪许的创造力是关于铜球和吊丝的，不是关于引力的。（22:12）
做实验几乎全部的功夫都在研究误差。他在卡文迪许实验室看单原子量子比特实验，满墙都是误差曲线。坏实验通常会给出你期望的结果。Brett 举了 UFO 目击，Naval 举了室温超导的闹剧。（24:15）

量子理论

其他三根支柱的误解来自公众，量子理论的误解则源自物理学家内部。早期创始人的小圈子接受了一种带神秘色彩的实证主义，之后又有同行压力、权威压力和压制学生提问。他猜公众现在对多世界的理解可能比多数物理学家还好。（26:19、28:19）
多重宇宙是量子理论里最不令人意外的部分，纠缠更反直觉。相对论比平行宇宙更反直觉：平行宇宙容易拍成电影，弯曲时空很难。（30:19）

支柱之间的衍生概念

四根支柱没有一根是他发明的，支柱之间的连接他只发明了一条（计算与量子）。“已知的万物理论”还缺意识、创造力和知识的来源。
他在《The Fabric of Reality》里关于自由意志和多重宇宙的说法”不充分，甚至可能误导”。多重宇宙没有解决自由意志问题，只是让反事实有了意义。（34:20）
“物理决定了没有自由意志”是在误用物理。热力学第二定律在单个分子层面也不存在，但它是硬科学。科学知识存在于多个涌现层次。（36:20）
多米诺骨牌的例子：你能预测哪块不会倒，却不知道原因是质数。预测不等于解释。（40:21）
自由意志的关键是创造新解释。爱因斯坦写下广义相对论，是从无到有，此前它不隐含在任何地方。它不可预测，不是因为随机，而恰恰相反：它是那个具体问题的解。想一个”随机数”是自由意志的反面。（42:22、44:23）
Hilbert 听完爱因斯坦的讲座后写出了场方程，却不懂自己写的是什么。
知识是物理变换所必需的一种信息，这是 constructor theory 的表述。目前已知能创造知识的只有进化和人的思考。（48:24）
财富是一个人能实现的物理变换的集合，所以不能用一个数字衡量。莫扎特和 Nathan Rothschild 谁更富，没法比较。（50:25）
“爱因斯坦只是在重组已有知识”，就像说”人只是原子”。你现在也去重组试试。（52:28）→ Creativity is not just recombination
乐观原则的另一种表述：没有人，能实现的物理变换只剩几十种（各类恒星之类）。几乎所有可能的变换都只能由创造知识的人来实现。（54:30）
Constructor theory 不用”初始条件加运动定律”，而是描述哪些变换可能、哪些不可能。达尔文解释了大象，而不是预测了大象。（56:32）

进步不是必然的

被问到技术乐观主义和加速主义里的”必然性”时，他说把进步看成必然很危险，会让人忽视风险。结果取决于我们，雅典和佛罗伦萨都衰落了。Brett 补充：必然论其实藏着悲观，因为它把人当成只是搭顺风车的。（1:08:37）→ Progress is possible but not inevitable
想改善世界和想过好生活是同一个问题。Borlaug、Faraday、Newton 都是在解决自己觉得有意思的问题，不是先挑”最重要的问题”。偏离这一点是危险的。（1:10:37）

Progress is possible but not inevitable
Creativity is not just recombination
An experiment chooses between rival explanations
Choose problems that are fun whether or not you solve them

sources/Naval---The-Deutsch-Files-III.title: The Deutsch Files III
sources/Naval---The-Deutsch-Files-III.content:
Summary
本集最集中地讨论了”创造力是什么、不是什么”：它不只是重组，也不同于生物进化，因为它能跳过缺口。接着讨论 AGI 复制是否会导致爆炸、Taking Children Seriously 面对的两个强反驳（不可逆的危险、大脑可塑性）、双胞胎研究，以及 Deutsch 自己的”狂想”（怎样让程序续写莫扎特）和对”终极解释”的拒绝。

参与者：Naval、Brett Hall、David Deutsch
时长：59:19

Key Takeaways
证明

有记者引用他说过”波普尔证明了 AI 不能超级智能”，他否认。对一个无法定义的东西，不可能证明任何事。
数学和其他领域的区别在研究对象，不在获得知识的方式。数学研究必然真理，但数学发现仍然是猜想，猜的是”这是必然真理”。（0:00、2:02）

创造力

Jobs 那句”创造力就是把东西组合起来”，错的只有”就是”两个字，就像说”人就是原子”。一千年前和今天的曼哈顿岛，差别只能用创造力解释。没有任何自然过程会产生摩天大楼。（4:02）→ Creativity is not just recombination
进化也不”只是”重组，它是变异加选择。翼龙的飞行能力不存在于任何祖先里，它是新的。
人的猜想不只更快，而且是解释性的，所以能跳过无法一步步走过去的缺口。进化必须每一步都活着，因此永远进化不出偏转小行星的系统。工程师可以一句话提出”把尾翼做成一整块”，先在脑子里批评，不必造出一串飞不起来的飞机。这就是通用性：能到达任何想法，并批评它。（8:04、10:06）→ Explanatory creativity can cross gaps that evolution cannot
Brett 的补充：如果从外星看地球，小行星被偏转开就是智能存在的证据；承载知识的信息比任何物理对象都更持久。Deutsch 说莎士比亚第 18 首十四行诗说的也是这件事（“So long lives this”），Naval 则提到了《奥兹曼迪亚斯》。（12:07）

AGI 复制

算力不是免费的。复制一个 AGI，要么内存和处理器减半，要么得买一台新电脑，而且电脑应该归 AGI 所有，否则它就是奴隶。这不会导致爆炸。投票权之类的制度问题，稍加调整就能解决。（16:09）

Taking Children Seriously

反驳一：有些行为不可逆，比如芬太尼和意外怀孕。回应：你举的这些，恰恰是在”可以对孩子无限使用强制”的现行制度下出名的问题。所以你得额外论证”把人当人”会让情况更糟。说服不了别人，是因为知识不足。刻板印象里的孩子”既无限轻信，又无限抗拒说理”。（18:09、22:10）
学习永远是学习者自己头脑中的创造行为。现行教育制度公开地以灌输服从和复制现有理论为目标。如果成功了，最好的结果也是停滞。
多数反对学校的家长，其实仍然相信”水桶论”，只是嫌学校往桶里倒了坏东西。他主张的是：“关掉的是强迫，不是互动。”
反驳二：大脑可塑性。回应：现行教育恰恰是在浪费可塑性，因为它让所有人都有相同的想法。好学校应该宣传”我们让你的孩子变得各不相同”。可塑性不被教育占用，并不等于没被使用。（26:11、28:13）
推动教育更自由的理由不是培养天才，而是孩子是人。

建议与先天/后天

没有通用的建议。“做你喜欢的事”没有用，因为人本来就在做喜欢的事。要了解对方的问题情境。例子：Hugh Everett 12 岁时给爱因斯坦写信，爱因斯坦回了。（38:17）
双胞胎研究只在你已经相信”水桶论”时才有说服力。长得像的人会被别人用类似的方式对待。天生的模式识别能力强，反而可能让父母担心孩子太痴迷积木，逼他出去玩。思想内容主要是自己创造的：同一部纪录片，一百万人看了，只有你因此想成为 Faraday。（40:17、42:18）

Deutsch 的狂想

AGI 不会靠堆算力实现。如果他知道怎么做，今天就能在自己的电脑上写出来。所以他警惕按算力来监管 AGI。（48:19）
让程序去猜莫扎特的问题情境，而不是在他已有作品的空间里合成新曲子。莫扎特的下一部杰作一定能认出是他写的，但又是新的：认得出狮子的爪子，但那是一个新的证明。（50:22）
历史学家可以研究”乐观的历史”，比如雅典和佛罗伦萨。

终极解释与群体

要放弃”终极解释”的想法：一旦有了终极解释，理解世界的乐趣就到头了。科学看的恰恰是最大的图景。以为意识就是”进入某种快乐状态”的人，才是只盯着细节。宗教和神秘主义能让一部分人快乐，但只握着”一丝真理”，比如”国际象棋像音乐和爱一样能让人快乐”。（54:22）
Naval 和 Brett 都不愿加入以”批判理性主义”命名的群体。一旦成为群体，维持团结就压倒了追求真理。Deutsch 说：“我完全同意。“（58:25）

Extracted Notes

Creativity is not just recombination
Explanatory creativity can cross gaps that evolution cannot
Choose problems that are fun whether or not you solve them

sources/Naval---The-Deutsch-Files-IV.title: The Deutsch Files IV
sources/Naval---The-Deutsch-Files-IV.content:
Summary
前半段讲物理：四根支柱怎样连成一体（涌现、多重宇宙中的知识晶体），constructor theory 的动机和进展（热力学第一定律、时间），以及量子计算机真正的起源（为了检验 Everett）。后半段讲文化：反理性模因为什么存在，为什么教育是西方最反理性的制度，如何看待学校、7+5、Frederick Douglass，以及英国当下的言论与移民问题。从谈到工党执政推断，录制时间在 2024 年英国大选之后。

参与者：Naval、Brett Hall、David Deutsch
时长：1:25:06

Key Takeaways
物理与涌现

物理学家自牛顿以来习惯自下而上地理解世界，因此把热力学、认识论这些涌现理论看成”洗衣机理论”。他主张把还原论和整体论”装进一个袋子扎起来”：排除一套理论的唯一标准是它不是好解释。（0:00）
“根本”的意思是解释需要它，所以人对宇宙是根本的。什么是真实的，也看解释里是否需要它：物理定律你绊不倒，但它们是真实的。（4:02）
Dawkins 的”中间世界”论（人脑只为非洲草原进化）被通用性反驳：我们照样理解类星体和亚原子粒子。
知识是能靠纠错维持自身存在的信息。每个真理对应许多种错误，所以在纠错发生的区域，原本不同的宇宙会变得相似，形成晶体。（6:02）

Constructor theory

它像 Feynman 说的”棋盘规则”：只知道规则，理解不了棋局。（8:03）
他写第一篇论文时列了 18 条动机，其中包括：为什么需要初始条件的理论，却不需要终态的理论？（10:03）
Chiara Marletto 版本的热力学，第一定律也和信息有关，还自动给出能量下界，无需另加假设。（12:03）
时间理论的线索：Wheeler–DeWitt → Page–Wootters（静态宇宙靠纠缠产生时间）→ 他和 Chiara 的 constructor theory 版本。Constructor theory 必须是决定论的。“随机理论”说某事更可能发生，就像说它”魔法更多”，这句话本身推不出任何东西。（14:03、16:05）
他再次承认，《The Fabric of Reality》里说多重宇宙解决了自由意志，那是暗示错了。它只是提供了思考自由意志的框架，constructor theory 里反事实的意义更丰富。Constructor theory 本身也可能只是 21 世纪初的一个注脚。（18:05）
他不信任宣布自己”将要发明什么”的人，更喜欢听”这是我要处理的问题，不知道会走到哪”。这是波普尔主义者的”劣势”，但为事情本身去做的人往往才有进展。（20:05）

量子计算机的起源

他最初想的是检验 Everett，不是发明量子计算机。当时的共识是 Everett 与坍缩理论的实验预测相同，他认为不对。如果对方主张观察者导致坍缩，那就造一个自身不会退相干的观察者，也就是跑在量子计算机上的 AGI。那篇论文先被以”这是哲学”拒稿，后来与通用量子计算机的论文同时发表。（22:05、24:05）
另一条来源：Charlie Bennett 对他说”硬件就是物理”，他于是回家用量子物理重写了图灵的分析。
同一宇宙内部也有趋同进化，但多重宇宙里的趋同更系统。（28:05）

反理性模因

从石器到真正的进步用了 30 万年，这只能用反理性模因解释。我们不该惊讶：生物体内最稳定的是遗传密码，所有演化都朝更高保真的方向。物种灭绝大多是因为纠错太强、进化太慢，就像孔雀尾巴那样。（30:06、32:08）
创造力不可能是为了创造而进化出来的。波普尔指出不存在”从外部的指令”：文化没法像 DNA 那样直接复制，下一代只能去猜。
Matt Ridley 认为进步需要足够的人口规模。他不同意，反例是雅典。以往的启蒙都只持续了一两代，被”坏人赢了”终结。（34:09）
西方最反理性的是教育。核糖体是细胞的教育机构，20 亿年几乎没有进化。文化里负责保真传递的是教育机构，所以它天生反理性。真正的谜团是其他领域为什么越来越理性。（38:11、40:12）→ Education is the most anti-rational institution because it exists to transmit faithfully
Naval 提到”任何机构的行为，最好解释为被它的敌人把持”。Deutsch 反问：如果真是这样，进步从何而来？
言论自由并没有像中世纪行会那样被剥夺，现在的问题是时尚、风潮。语言仍然是通用的。如果”滑坡”是一条规律，就不会有启蒙。（44:14）
纠错能力强的系统会犯更大的错误，而其中的大错会被纠正。Naval 补充了前提：不能有人改动系统本身、让它停止纠错。Deutsch 同意，说这时要用次一级的纠错手段去阻止。1945 年艾德礼政府在经济上”功能性共产主义”，但坚定亲英，还说服美国加入北约。（50:16）→ Preserving the means of error correction is the heart of morality

教育

教育的做法变了（不再打孩子），但背后的理论仍是史前的”水桶论”：知识被倒进去，任何不忠实都是错误。这就像”监狱条件改善了”。过去一百年教育里的好改进几乎都来自左派，而他们的动机恰恰是认为文化不该被传递。（52:17）
母语和走路从来不是学校教的。如果在学校教走路，孩子到十岁还有一半不会走。（54:17）
7+5：孩子真的遇到问题（衣柜能放几双鞋）时，自己很快就能解决。先修课程是神话，跳过五年级直接进六年级，很快就能跟上。（56:19、1:00:20）
斯皮尔伯格的电影能吸引 90% 的孩子，不点名也不考试，但他也做不到让孩子每天都去。几乎所有孩子都想要 iPhone，而 iPhone 没有课程表。（1:02:21）
Frederick Douglass：奴隶少年在田里累了一天，冒着被鞭打的风险偷偷去学认字。今天他们的后代却被说成”必须被强迫才肯学”。这才是人本来的样子。（1:04:23）
过渡办法：1950 年代的学校回不去了，但恢复 1950 年代的国家课程是政府做得到的。“woke 不是一种理论，对解释的否定不是解释。“（1:12:25）

英国

阿尔巴尼亚在二战中救下了几乎所有犹太人，这是”穆斯林移民必然激进化”这一叙事的反例。第二代激进化是英国多元文化政策的错，不是伊斯兰的错。Deutsch 以二代移民的身份说，父母的态度是”我们欠周围的文化，而不是它欠我们”。（1:16:27）
英国的纠错不只有选举，还有公务员体系的惰性和报纸。移民是解决人口问题的明显办法，只要别让恨这个国家的人进来。（1:20:29）

Extracted Notes

Education is the most anti-rational institution because it exists to transmit faithfully
Preserving the means of error correction is the heart of morality

Naval treats get-rich-quick promises as a signal that the seller’s real business is selling hope. Durable wealth usually comes from a long compounding process, not a packaged shortcut.
Key Takeaways

Easy riches are usually someone else’s monetization strategy.
Credibility collapses when wealth advice depends on selling magical shortcuts.
Real progress can include good advice, but not promises of instant transformation.
Time horizon is part of intellectual honesty.

Time-for-money work stays linear.
Ownership is what allows non-linear upside.
Even high earners remain capped if they only sell hours.
Brand, IP, and equity let effort compound beyond the present moment.

sources/Paul-Graham---Keep-Your-Identity.filePath: sources/Paul Graham - Keep Your Identity Small.md
sources/Paul-Graham---Keep-Your-Identity.title: Keep Your Identity Small
sources/Paul-Graham---Keep-Your-Identity.content:
February 2009
I finally realized today why politics and religion yield such uniquely useless discussions.
As a rule, any mention of religion on an online forum degenerates into a religious argument. Why? Why does this happen with religion and not with Javascript or baking or other topics people talk about on forums?
What’s different about religion is that people don’t feel they need to have any particular expertise to have opinions about it. All they need is strongly held beliefs, and anyone can have those. No thread about Javascript will grow as fast as one about religion, because people feel they have to be over some threshold of expertise to post comments about that. But on religion everyone’s an expert.
Then it struck me: this is the problem with politics too. Politics, like religion, is a topic where there’s no threshold of expertise for expressing an opinion. All you need is strong convictions.
Do religion and politics have something in common that explains this similarity? One possible explanation is that they deal with questions that have no definite answers, so there’s no back pressure on people’s opinions. Since no one can be proven wrong, every opinion is equally valid, and sensing this, everyone lets fly with theirs.
But this isn’t true. There are certainly some political questions that have definite answers, like how much a new government policy will cost. But the more precise political questions suffer the same fate as the vaguer ones.
I think what religion and politics have in common is that they become part of people’s identity, and people can never have a fruitful argument about something that’s part of their identity. By definition they’re partisan.
Which topics engage people’s identity depends on the people, not the topic. For example, a discussion about a battle that included citizens of one or more of the countries involved would probably degenerate into a political argument. But a discussion today about a battle that took place in the Bronze Age probably wouldn’t. No one would know what side to be on. So it’s not politics that’s the source of the trouble, but identity.
When people say a discussion has degenerated into a religious war, what they really mean is that it has started to be driven mostly by people’s identities. [1]
Because the point at which this happens depends on the people rather than the topic, it’s a mistake to conclude that because a question tends to provoke religious wars, it must have no answer. For example, the question of the relative merits of programming languages often degenerates into a religious war, because so many programmers identify as X programmers or Y programmers. This sometimes leads people to conclude the question must be unanswerable—that all languages are equally good.
Obviously that’s false: anything else people make can be well or badly designed; why should this be uniquely impossible for programming languages? And indeed, you can have a fruitful discussion about the relative merits of programming languages, so long as you exclude people who respond from identity.
More generally, you can have a fruitful discussion about a topic only if it doesn’t engage the identities of any of the participants. What makes politics and religion such minefields is that they engage so many people’s identities. But you could in principle have a useful conversation about them with some people. And there are other topics that might seem harmless, like the relative merits of Ford and Chevy pickup trucks, that you couldn’t safely talk about with others.
The most intriguing thing about this theory, if it’s right, is that it explains not merely which kinds of discussions to avoid, but how to have better ideas. If people can’t think clearly about anything that has become part of their identity, then all other things being equal, the best plan is to let as few things into your identity as possible. [2]
Most people reading this will already be fairly tolerant. But there is a step beyond thinking of yourself as x but tolerating y: not even to consider yourself an x. The more labels you have for yourself, the dumber they make you.
Notes
[1] When that happens, it tends to happen fast, like a core going critical. The threshold for participating goes down to zero, which brings in more people. And they tend to say incendiary things, which draw more and angrier counterarguments.
[2] There may be some things it’s a net win to include in your identity. For example, being a scientist. But arguably that is more of a placeholder than an actual label—like putting NMI on a form that asks for your middle initial—because it doesn’t commit you to believing anything in particular. A scientist isn’t committed to believing in natural selection in the same way a biblical literalist is committed to rejecting it. All he’s committed to is following the evidence wherever it leads.
Considering yourself a scientist is equivalent to putting a sign in a cupboard saying “this cupboard must be kept empty.” Yes, strictly speaking, you’re putting something in the cupboard, but not in the ordinary sense.
Thanks to Sam Altman, Trevor Blackwell, Paul Buchheit, and Robert Morris for reading drafts of this.

sources/Paul-Graham---保持小身份.title: 保持小身份
sources/Paul-Graham---保持小身份.content:
2009 年 2 月
今天，我终于明白了为什么政治和宗教总会引发格外无效的讨论。
一般来说，只要有人在网络论坛上提到宗教，讨论就会退化成宗教争论。为什么？为什么宗教会如此，而 JavaScript、烘焙或其他论坛话题却不会？
宗教的特别之处在于，人们并不觉得自己必须具备某种专业知识才有资格发表意见。他们只需要拥有坚定的信念，而任何人都能拥有信念。讨论 JavaScript 的帖子不会像宗教帖那样迅速膨胀，因为人们觉得，自己的专业水平必须达到某个门槛才能发表评论。但在宗教问题上，每个人都是专家。
接着我突然意识到：政治也存在同样的问题。和宗教一样，政治也是一个不需要达到任何专业门槛就能发表意见的话题。你只需要有坚定的立场。
宗教和政治是否具有某种共同点，足以解释这种相似性？一种可能的解释是，它们讨论的问题没有确定答案，因此人们的意见不会受到现实的反向约束。既然谁都无法被证明是错的，每种意见就都同样有效；人们感受到这一点，便纷纷畅所欲言。
但事实并非如此。有些政治问题显然存在确定答案，例如一项新的政府政策需要花费多少钱。然而，更精确的政治问题仍然会遭遇和模糊问题一样的命运。
我认为，宗教和政治的共同之处在于，它们会成为人们身份认同的一部分。对于已经成为自身身份一部分的事物，人们永远无法进行富有成果的争论。按照定义，他们已经站队了。
什么话题会触及身份认同，取决于参与者，而不是话题本身。例如，如果一场战争的讨论中有来自参战国家的公民，它很可能会退化成政治争论。但如果讨论的是一场发生在青铜时代的战争，今天大概就不会如此。没有人知道自己该站在哪一边。因此，问题的根源不是政治，而是身份认同。
当人们说一场讨论已经退化成“宗教战争”时，他们真正的意思是：讨论开始主要由参与者的身份认同所驱动。[1]
由于这种转变发生的临界点取决于参与者，而非话题本身，因此，不能因为一个问题经常引发宗教战争，就断定它必然没有答案。例如，关于编程语言优劣的讨论经常退化成宗教战争，因为许多程序员把自己认同为 X 程序员或 Y 程序员。这有时会让人们误以为，这个问题不可能有答案——所有语言都同样优秀。
这显然是错的：人类制造的其他事物都可能设计得好或坏，为什么编程语言偏偏不可能如此？事实上，只要排除那些从身份认同出发作答的人，我们完全可以富有成果地讨论不同编程语言的相对优劣。
更一般地说，只有当一个话题不会触及任何参与者的身份认同时，讨论才可能富有成果。政治和宗教之所以处处是雷区，是因为它们会触及太多人的身份认同。但原则上，你仍然可以和某些人就这些话题进行有益的交流。另一方面，有些看起来无害的话题，例如福特和雪佛兰皮卡谁更好，却可能无法和另一些人安全地讨论。
如果这个理论是正确的，那么最耐人寻味之处在于：它不仅解释了我们应该避开哪些讨论，也解释了怎样才能产生更好的想法。如果人们无法清晰思考任何已经成为自身身份一部分的事物，那么在其他条件相同的情况下，最好的策略就是尽量少让事物进入自己的身份认同。[2]
读到这里的大多数人可能已经相当宽容。但在“把自己看作 X，同时容忍 Y”之外，还可以再进一步：根本不把自己看作 X。你给自己贴的标签越多，它们就会让你变得越愚蠢。
注释
[1] 一旦这种情况发生，往往会发展得非常快，就像堆芯达到临界状态。参与讨论的门槛会降到零，从而吸引更多人加入。而他们往往会说出煽动性的话，又引来更多、更愤怒的反驳。
[2] 或许有些事物纳入身份认同后，整体上是有益的。例如，把自己视为科学家。但可以说，这更像一个占位符，而不是真正的标签——就像在要求填写中间名首字母的表格中填上 NMI（无中间名首字母）。因为它并不要求你承诺相信任何特定观点。科学家对自然选择的信奉，并不像《圣经》字面主义者对否定自然选择的坚持。科学家唯一承诺的是：证据指向哪里，就跟随到哪里。
把自己视为科学家，就像在一个橱柜里放上一块牌子，写着“这个橱柜必须保持空置”。严格来说，你确实往橱柜里放了东西，但并不是通常意义上的那种“放东西”。
感谢 Sam Altman、Trevor Blackwell、Paul Buchheit 和 Robert Morris 阅读本文草稿。

sources/Pryzant-et-al.---Automatic-Promp.filePath: sources/Pryzant et al. - Automatic Prompt Optimization with Gradient Descent and Beam Search.md
sources/Pryzant-et-al.---Automatic-Promp.title: Automatic Prompt Optimization with Gradient Descent and Beam Search
sources/Pryzant-et-al.---Automatic-Promp.content:
Summary
Pryzant et al. introduce ProTeGi / APO, a black-box prompt optimization method that uses LLM-generated natural-language critiques as “textual gradients.” The method evaluates a prompt on minibatches, asks an LLM to describe why the prompt failed, edits the prompt in the opposite semantic direction, and uses beam search plus bandit selection to retain promising candidates.
Key Takeaways

APO reframes prompt tuning as a measurable optimization loop over validation data, not as open-ended prompt brainstorming.
Natural-language gradients preserve interpretability because every optimization step can be inspected as a critique and an edit.
Beam search and bandit selection make the search more efficient than undirected prompt mutation.
The method assumes a clear task metric, a seed prompt, representative training examples, and access to an LLM API.
The reported gains show that vague task descriptions can be rewritten into more precise annotation instructions automatically.

Local PDF
Extracted Notes

Textual gradients make prompt errors editable in natural language
Prompt optimization turns prompt writing into measurable search
APO quality depends on validation data and metric design

sources/Ramnath-et-al.---A-Systematic-Su.title: A Systematic Survey of Automatic Prompt Optimization Techniques
sources/Ramnath-et-al.---A-Systematic-Su.content:
Summary
Ramnath et al. provide an EMNLP 2025 survey of APO methods. They define automatic prompt optimization formally, then organize the field around a five-part anatomy: seed prompts, inference evaluation and feedback, candidate generation, candidate filtering, and iteration depth.
Key Takeaways

The paper is a practical field guide for black-box APO systems where model weights are unavailable.
Its taxonomy separates prompt initialization, feedback, edit generation, candidate selection, and stopping criteria.
APO is positioned as useful because prompts remain brittle across task descriptions, ordering, phrasing, and formatting.
The survey distinguishes APE as a specific method from APO as the broader area.
This is the best entry point for mapping the APO literature before reading individual methods.

sources/Rey-Su---Student-for-life.title: student for life
sources/Rey-Su---Student-for-life.content:
Summary
Rey Su argues that the most useful stable identity is not a fixed career plan but a willingness to keep learning through internships, side projects, uncertainty, and repeated career changes.
Key Takeaways

Genuine curiosity makes it easier to learn from other people.
A student mindset can hold together periods of career uncertainty.
Lower living costs can create room for learning-rich but risky work.

sources/Rich-Sutton---The-Bitter-Lesson.title: The Bitter Lesson
sources/Rich-Sutton---The-Bitter-Lesson.content:
Summary
Rich Sutton’s short essay argues that the biggest lesson from 70 years of AI research is that general methods that leverage computation are ultimately the most effective, by a large margin, because the cost of computation keeps falling exponentially. He walks through computer chess, computer Go, speech recognition, and computer vision, where each time researchers who built in human knowledge of the domain won in the short term and were overtaken once search and learning could be run at scale. The lesson is “bitter” because the winning approach is a rejection of the human-centric one researchers favored. Fetched directly from the original URL on 2026-10-28; read in full.
Key Takeaways

Most AI research is conducted as if the available computation were constant, but over a slightly longer time than a typical research project, “massively more computation inevitably becomes available.”
Human-knowledge approaches and computation-leveraging approaches “need not run counter to each other, but in practice they tend to”: time spent on one is not spent on the other, and built-in knowledge complicates methods so they use general computation less well.
The pattern repeats across fields: chess (Kasparov, 1997: deep search over human-informed methods), Go (about 20 years later: search plus self-play learning), speech recognition (1970s DARPA contest: HMM statistics over phoneme and vocal-tract knowledge; later deep learning), and vision (edges, generalized cylinders, SIFT replaced by convolution and a few invariances).
The four-step historical observation: researchers build knowledge in; it helps in the short term and is personally satisfying; in the long run it plateaus and even inhibits progress; breakthroughs arrive from scaling computation by search and learning.
First lesson: general-purpose methods that “continue to scale with increased computation even as the available computation becomes very great.” The two that scale arbitrarily are search and learning.
Second lesson: the contents of minds are “tremendously, irredeemably complex,” so we should build in only meta-methods that can find and capture that complexity, not our own discoveries: “We want AI agents that can discover like we can, not which contain what we have discovered.”

Extracted Notes

General methods that keep scaling with computation beat human-knowledge methods in the long run
Built-in human knowledge helps in the short term and then plateaus
Search and learning are the two methods that scale with arbitrary computation
AI should be built to discover rather than to contain what we have discovered
Researchers resist the bitter lesson because building in knowledge is satisfying and pays off early

Related

Commonly cited in Stanford CS336 - Lecture 01 - Overview, Tokenization, which reads it as “algorithms that scale matter”, not “scale alone matters.”

sources/Spiess-et-al.---AutoPDL-Automati.title: AutoPDL Automatic Prompt Optimization for LLM Agents
sources/Spiess-et-al.---AutoPDL-Automati.content:
Summary
Spiess et al. propose AutoPDL, an AutoML-style optimizer for LLM agent configurations. Instead of optimizing only prompt wording, AutoPDL jointly searches prompting patterns such as zero-shot, CoT, ReAct, and ReWOO, plus instructions and demonstrations, then outputs executable and editable PDL programs.
Key Takeaways

Agent prompt optimization must search over both prompt content and the surrounding prompting pattern.
The final artifact is source code in PDL, not just an opaque winning prompt string.
Successive halving is used to navigate a combinatorial space of patterns, examples, and instructions.
The best prompting pattern varies by model and task, so fixed agent templates can leave performance on the table.
Human-readable prompt programs make post-optimization review and reuse more realistic.

Prompt optimization turns prompt writing into measurable search

sources/Stanford-CS336---Lecture-01---Ov.title: Stanford CS336 Lecture 1 - Overview, Tokenization
sources/Stanford-CS336---Lecture-01---Ov.content:
Summary
Percy Liang opens the third edition of CS336 by arguing why researchers should understand language models at the level of implementation rather than prompting, and what parts of that understanding survive the gap between classroom scale and frontier scale. The bulk of the lecture is a walkthrough of the five course units — basics, systems, scaling laws, data, and alignment — each mapped to one assignment. The final third starts the first technical unit, tokenization, building up from character- and byte-level schemes to byte-pair encoding. The through-line for the whole course is efficiency: getting the best model out of a fixed compute and data budget.
Key Takeaways

Results at small scale do not always transfer: the share of FLOPs spent in MLP layers rises from roughly 44% at small scale to about 80% at 175B, and few-shot capabilities only appear past a critical scale, so attention-level optimizations validated on small models may not pay off at the frontier.
The course splits transferable knowledge into mechanics (how a transformer or model parallelism works), mindset (profile and benchmark everything, take scaling seriously), and intuitions (which data and modeling choices work). Mechanics and mindset transfer; intuitions largely do not, which is why some design choices are only justified by experiment — the SwiGLU paper famously attributes its gains to “divine benevolence.”
The bitter lesson is commonly misread as “scale is all that matters.” The correct reading is that algorithms which scale are what matter: accuracy is roughly efficiency times resources, and efficiency matters more as budgets grow, since a 5% gain on a $100M run is significant. See Rich Sutton - The Bitter Lesson and General methods that keep scaling with computation beat human-knowledge methods in the long run.
Frontier models are closed — the GPT-4 report explicitly declines to describe how the model was built — so the course depends on the open ecosystem (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek) and on fully open efforts such as AI2, NVIDIA, and the Marin project that release data and code alongside weights.
Assignments: A1 implements BPE, the transformer, loss, and optimizer, with perplexity leaderboards on TinyStories and OpenWebText; A2 covers Triton kernels and parallelism; A3 fits scaling laws against a cached training API that returns a loss for a submitted config; A4 filters and deduplicates a raw web crawl; A5 covers alignment with DPO and GRPO.
A tokenizer’s compression ratio is bytes per token, and raising it shortens sequences, which matters because attention is quadratic in sequence length. Character-level tokenization wastes a 150k-entry Unicode vocabulary on rare characters; byte-level gives a 256-entry vocabulary but a compression ratio of 1; word-level gives an unbounded vocabulary and needs an UNK token.
BPE starts from a byte sequence where every byte is a token, repeatedly finds the most frequent adjacent pair, and merges it into a new token id starting at 256. It originated in data compression, moved to neural machine translation, and was first used for LLMs in GPT-2. Common sequences become single tokens and rare ones fall back to smaller units, so nothing is out of vocabulary.
Tokenizers are awkward in practice: a word and the same word with a leading space are unrelated token ids, digit grouping is often unpredictable, and multilingual vocabularies now run to 100k–200k tokens, trading compression against sparsity.
Any end-to-end replacement for tokenization would still need the two properties a tokenizer provides — abstraction above raw bytes, since individual bytes are low signal-to-noise, and variable-size chunks so that compute is spent adaptively.
